title: From Event Logs to Governed Action: A BlueSky Agenda for Agentic Process Mining
abstract: Process mining has long turned event logs into process knowledge: discovered models, conformance evidence, bottleneck diagnoses, and runtime predictions. Agentic AI changes the target. Process-aware agents will not only ask what happened. They will ask whether a proposed action should be taken, given the available evidence, privacy budget, organizational authority, and downstream risk. This BlueSky paper proposes event-to-action process mining: a process-mining agenda for transforming heterogeneous operational event data into governed action. The goal is not another dashboard, a generic enterprise simulator, or a language interface over logs. We argue that the community needs four mineable artifacts: event-object representations, action evidence packages, governance contracts, and benchmarks where act, defer, ask, and refuse are all valid outputs. This agenda is timely because agentic business process management (BPM), LLM-assisted process mining, object-centric event standards, causal process monitoring, and privacy-preserving learning are maturing separately. Bringing them together defines a data-mining target inside process mining: mining logged organizational behavior for accountable action, not only retrospective insight.

title: The Neighbor Graph of Linear Complementary Dual (LCD) Codes
abstract: Linear complementary dual (LCD) codes form an important class of linear codes with applications in cryptography, classical error correction, and quantum coding theory. In this paper, we study the neighbor relation on LCD codes over finite fields and the graph induced by this relation, where two codes are adjacent whenever they intersect in codimension one. We determine the number of neighbors of an LCD code that are also LCD, and we use this result to analyze the structure of the corresponding neighbor graph. In particular, we prove its regularity over arbitrary finite fields and establish further regularity properties for its main structural subgraphs in the binary and odd-characteristic cases. These results provide a graph-theoretic framework for the study of LCD codes and reveal a strong combinatorial regularity in their neighborhood structure.

title: From Explicit References to Scene Manifolds: Distributional Fidelity and Realism for Radiance Field Quality Assessment
abstract: Radiance field representations such as 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enable high-quality novel view synthesis but can introduce complex, view-dependent artifacts from reconstruction, rendering, and compression. Reliable perceptual quality assessment (QA) is thus essential for evaluating rendered views and guiding the design of perceptually faithful scene representations. Existing full-reference QA metrics require an aligned reference image, while recent cross-reference metrics relax this requirement by comparing a test view with non-aligned references. However, under wide-baseline radiance field settings, selecting a reliable nearby reference can be difficult, particularly when evaluating views along arbitrary trajectories and poses. We propose SCODA, a lightweight scene-conditioned objective QA method that shifts QA from explicit image-to-image comparison to scene-manifold modeling. High-quality observations of each scene are represented as a multivariate Gaussian distribution in deep feature space, producing a semantic fidelity score that measures deviation from the scene distribution. A weakly-supervised distortion-aware patch discriminator provides a complementary realism signal, and both cues are combined through an unsupervised bounded fusion strategy. Experiments on multiple benchmarks show strong agreement with human judgments and robust generalization across GS- and NeRF-generated views and trajectories. Code is publicly available at https://gitlab.com/saeedmp/scoda.

title: VST: Verifiable Structured Transport for Auditable Agent-to-Agent Alpha Discovery
abstract: Agent-to-agent (A2A) alpha discovery is slowed by repeated feedback cycles between mining and evaluation agents, whose hand-offs, in contemporary LLM multi-agent systems, are free-form natural-language messages that carry no stable contract and cannot be replayed. We first restructure this communication as a structured agent-to-agent protocol of \emph{typed, causally addressable, unicast records}, so that the committed stream forms a causal trajectory. On that trajectory a single predictor with four typed heads forecasts the accumulated guidance the two miners would receive several cycles ahead; a transactional verify--leap controller then commits a multi-cycle speculative outcome only when it passes a four-level gate, and otherwise rolls back to the exact prior state. Structure is the enabling contribution, and its value is not accuracy. A controlled ablation shows an equal-information free-text channel reaches the same predictor hit rate. What typing provides is a state that can be schema-checked, replayed deterministically, and prevented by construction from leaking a forecast to an evaluator: auditability by construction, not an empirically stress-tested guarantee. On a CSI~1000 out-of-sample holdout, our single run is the only one among eight methods (seven baselines and ours) to hold a positive median annualized return and Sharpe at the factor level, though the median return \emph{in excess} of the benchmark stays negative for every method including ours; its development-selected top-20 portfolios reach a $0.71$ median holdout Sharpe, selected on a split inside the optimization horizon. We report these single-run results descriptively, gross of costs, and are explicit about their limits throughout; in particular we do not isolate the effect of the leap machinery from the inherited search substrate, which we leave to future work.

title: Disseny i caracterització experimental de desfasadors fotònics no volàtils basats en Sb2Se3 per a computació neuromòrfica
abstract: [EN] This work addresses the design, simulation, and experimental characterization of multilevel optical phase shifters based on antimony selenide (Sb2Se3) in silicon photonics. This phasechange material enables the non-volatile transition between crystalline and amorphous states, exhibiting a high refractive index contrast that facilitates the development of highly compact and low-energy-consumption devices. The work focuses on the design of the phase shifter and the experimental evaluation of the material's switching states using Mach-Zehnder interferometric structures. Furthermore, the material's reproducibility and the phase discrepancies relative to numerical simulations have been analyzed. Finally, the integration of the phase shifter as a synaptic weight in coherent photonic neural network architectures has been addressed.

title: Analyzing Intent Recognition and Prompt Reformulation in ChatGPT: A User Study
abstract: Data Collection The data collected with gpt-3.5-turbo-1106 and gpt-4-1106-preview are in the corresponding JSON files. User Study Design Our manuscript (10.1016/j.chbah.2026.100400) contains more information about the exact design of our study. Chat History To strive for an even data distribution and avoid "small talk" conversations, we provided a question-answer pair as chat history before the participants interacted with GPT and asked them to continue the conversations. The chat histories were selected from the Hugging Face dataset (Lhoest, Q., del Moral, A. V., Jernite, Y., Thakur, A., von Platen, P., Patil, S., ... & Wolf, T. (2021), available at: https://huggingface.co/datasets/P1ayer-1/chatgpt-conversations-chatlogs.net?row=46. We only worked with samples written in English. Datasets: A community library for natural language processing. arXiv preprint arXiv:2109.02846.). We selected 240 samples (10 per each fine-granular intent category). Each participant interacted with GPT 10 times during the study, where ten different fine-granular intent categories were selected randomly. The exact chat history question-answer pairs with the corresponding fine-granular intent category and is saved in the chat_history.json file for reproducibility. Prompting details for reproducibility: User Study Phase 1: Quality of Intent Recognition by State-of-the-Art LLMs The participants were introduced to conversational contexts extracted from a publicly accessible dataset (see Chat History) and were asked to continue these dialogues. The answer from the underlying LLM was generated with the prompt: 'Suppose that a user previously asked you the question (-history question-) and you gave the user this answer (-history answer-). Please answer the following question in a maximum 2500 characters: -user question-.' Then the LLM analyzed the user’s prompt to recognize their intent: 'Here is a conversation between the user (Anonymous) and the AI assistant (Chat GPT). Please analyze the potential intent of the user's upcoming question, and identify it as one of the following 24 categories. Please reply only with the category number (numeric) and the category name, and return only the most probable category. No explanation is needed. The 24 intent categories are as follows: [ 1. Factual Queries: Requests for specific facts or data; 2. Explanatory Inquiries: Explanations or clarifications about concepts, events, phenomena; 3. Tutorial Requests: Step-by-step instructions or guidance; 4. Troubleshooting Assistance: Diagnose and resolve issues or problems; 5. Decision Support: Assistance in decision-making through insights, comparisons, evaluations; 6. Planning and Organization: Aid in planning events, organizing tasks, or managing projects; 7. Idea Generation: Inspiration or ideas for creative projects; 8. Content Creation: Help in writing, visually representing, or designing original content; 9. Artistic Exploration: Exploration of artistic styles, techniques, historical art contexts; 10. Learning Support: Assistance with understanding educational material or concepts; 11. Skill Development: Guidance on developing specific skills or competencies; 12. Curricular Planning: Help in designing or choosing educational curricula or courses; 13. Conversational Engagement: Dialogue for entertainment, companionship, interaction; 14. Personal Advice: Advice on personal matters or life decisions. 15. Reflection and Insight: Help in self-reflection, personal growth, or to gain insights into certain behavior or thoughts; 16. Technical Guidance: Assistance with technical tasks, coding, or problem-solving in a professional context; 17. Business and Career Advice: Guidance on business, career choices, or professional development; 18. Industry-Specific Inquiries: Requests for information or assistance specific to certain industries or professional fields; 19. Service Utilization: Requests to use specific functionalities of the model (e.g., language translation, summarization); 20. Data Processing: Help in processing, analyzing, or visualizing data; 21. Task Automation: Inquiries about automating tasks or workflows; 22. Moral and Ethical Queries: Questions about ethical dilemmas, moral principles, or philosophical theories; 23. Societal and Cultural Inquiry: Exploring societal, cultural, or historical topics; 24. Existential Questions: Delving into existential themes or abstract philosophical questions] The conversation content is: User: -user question- ChatGPT: -GPT answer-' Lastly, the participants were then asked whether they agreed with the intent category identified by the LLM In cases where participants disagreed with the detected intent, they were asked to select a more suitable category from our intent taxonomy. User Study Phase 1: Effect of Intent-based Prompt Reformulation on User Satisfaction The underlying LLM generated one of the responses directly from the original user prompt, while the other response was generated based on the reformulated user prompt aligning with the correctly identified intent category. Before generating the response for the reformulated user input, a grammar check was conducted: 'Correct the following sentence grammatically: -user question-'. Then, the LLM response was generated with the prompt corresponding to the fine-granular intent category: 'Suppose that a user previously asked you the question (-history question-) and you gave the user this answer (-history answer-). Please answer the following question in a maximum 2500 characters, while taking the chat history into consideration: -prompt corresponding to the intent category- the user input: -grammatically correct user question-'. The original LLM answers were loaded from Phase 1. The order of the displayed answers was randomized, the first answer displayed over the 10 questions: original, original, reprompted, reprompted, reprompted, reprompted, original, reprompted, original, original.

title: Adaptive Algorithm Evolution Based on Multi-Agent Collaboration
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to algorithm evolution leveraging the principles of multi-agent collaboration and competition. The core idea is to create a system of multiple agents, each responsible for a specific aspect of algorithm evolution. These agents interact through both cooperation and competition, ultimately driving the optimization of the algorithm's performance. The proposed framework aims to enhance the adaptability and robustness of algorithms by mimicking the biological process of evolution and the collaborative dynamics observed in multi-agent systems. We explore the potential of this approach to address challenges in algorithm design and optimization, particularly in dynamic and uncertain environments. The key mathematical framework utilizes agent-based modeling, evolutionary game theory, and optimization techniques to formalize the interaction and evolution process. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of this collaborative approach in achieving adaptive algorithm evolution.

title: Self-Adaptive Geometry Models: A Chaotic Diffusion Approach
abstract: This paper investigates the application of chaotic diffusion mechanisms within self-adaptive geometric models to enhance prediction accuracy and generalization capabilities. Traditional geometric modeling approaches often rely on fixed parameters, limiting the model's flexibility. We propose a novel framework that dynamically introduces randomness through a chaotic diffusion process, resulting in more robust and adaptable models. This work explores the impact of this approach on various predictive tasks, demonstrating significant improvements in both precision and the model's ability to generalize to unseen data. The core mechanism leverages the inherent unpredictability of chaotic systems to provide a more comprehensive representation of the underlying data.

title: Adaptive Optimization Algorithm Topology Structure
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization framework based on adaptive optimization algorithm topology structure. The core innovation lies in dynamically adjusting the optimization algorithm's parameter set during the optimization process, allowing the algorithm to respond to data fluctuations and improve efficiency. We propose a method that iteratively adjusts the parameters based on observed data, resulting in a more robust and adaptable optimization strategy. This approach contrasts with static optimization techniques, offering a significant improvement in performance across various problem domains. The paper details the methodology, presents experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness, and concludes with a discussion of its potential applications and future research directions.

title: Explainable AI via Bayesian Knowledge Graphs
abstract: The increasing deployment of complex Artificial Intelligence (AI) models, particularly deep neural networks, has raised significant concerns about their "black-box" nature. Understanding *why* an AI model makes a specific prediction is crucial for trust, safety, and accountability. This paper proposes a novel approach to explainable AI (XAI) based on the construction and utilization of Bayesian Knowledge Graphs (BKGs). The core idea is to represent the learned knowledge within an AI model as a structured, probabilistic network, enabling us to trace the reasoning process behind decisions. We demonstrate that by mapping the model's internal representations into a BKG, we can provide probabilistic explanations for the model's outputs, quantifying the confidence associated with different parts of the knowledge graph. This approach offers a more intuitive and transparent way to understand AI models compared to traditional XAI methods. The paper outlines the methodology for building BKGs from AI models, discusses the key components of the graph, and presents a theoretical framework for reasoning with the graph. We also explore potential applications and future research directions. ---

title: 基于量子态的动态拓扑变换算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic topology transformation algorithm based on quantum state adaptation. Traditional topology transformation algorithms are often static, limiting their efficiency and generalization capabilities. We propose an algorithm that leverages quantum state dynamics to dynamically adjust transformation parameters during optimization, aiming to achieve superior local optima. The core of this approach is the implementation of a quantum-enhanced adaptation mechanism that continuously refines the transformation process, leading to improved solution quality. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this algorithm through a series of illustrative examples, showcasing its ability to overcome limitations of conventional methods. The algorithm's potential impact extends to a wide range of optimization problems, particularly those involving complex geometries and constraints.

title: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning with Memory Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to reinforcement learning (RL) that combines the strengths of hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) and memory networks. Traditional RL methods often struggle with complex tasks due to the curse of dimensionality and the difficulty of learning long-term dependencies. Hierarchical RL offers a solution by breaking down complex tasks into smaller, more manageable sub-tasks. However, it can still be inefficient in environments with sparse rewards and limited exploration. Memory networks provide a mechanism for storing and retrieving past experiences, which can significantly improve learning efficiency and enable agents to generalize to new situations. Our approach integrates these two techniques, creating an agent capable of both temporal abstraction and long-term memory. The core claim is that this combination allows agents to learn complex tasks effectively. The core mechanism involves a hierarchical structure where sub-tasks are learned, and memory networks store and retrieve relevant information to guide learning within each sub-task. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and a conceptual outline, highlighting its potential for improved learning performance in challenging RL environments. The key innovation lies in the synergistic interaction between the hierarchical decomposition and the memory network's ability to capture and utilize long-range dependencies.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Programming via Dynamic Bayesian Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for neuro-symbolic programming utilizing Dynamic Bayesian Networks (DBNs) to integrate the strengths of neural networks and symbolic reasoning. The core idea is to leverage neural networks for efficient feature extraction and then employ a DBN to encode and execute symbolic rules, continuously refining its knowledge base through probabilistic inference based on incoming sensory data. This approach aims to achieve robust and explainable decision-making in complex environments by combining the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks with the logical deduction power of DBNs. The system dynamically updates its internal representation, enabling adaptability to changing conditions and improved accuracy over time. The key innovation lies in the dynamic interaction between these two components, fostering a truly hybrid system. We define a formal model encompassing the key components and their interactions, outlining a methodology for building and training such a system. The proposed architecture addresses limitations of traditional approaches by providing a mechanism for transparent reasoning and continual learning. We demonstrate the potential of this framework through a conceptual design and outline key implementation considerations. ---

title: Dynamic Topology Quantum Computing Adaptive Learning Algorithm
abstract: Quantum computing offers the potential for unprecedented computational power, but realizing this potential requires overcoming fundamental limitations in existing computational paradigms. This paper introduces a novel dynamic topology quantum computing adaptive learning algorithm, designed to dynamically adjust quantum system parameters in response to environmental changes. Traditional machine learning algorithms rely on pre-defined models, while this approach leverages the inherent adaptability of quantum topology to achieve enhanced scalability and flexibility. The algorithm's core mechanism involves utilizing the self-adaptive nature of quantum topology to iteratively refine the quantum system's state, leading to improved performance in complex quantum computations. We present a comprehensive theoretical analysis and initial experimental validation demonstrating the algorithm's efficacy in solving specific quantum algorithms.

title: Typed Mathematics as Role-Preserving Structure An Extended Definition for Closure Theory
abstract: The typed architecture of a closure problem. The upper level shows the full system with history, action, dynamics, and observables. The lower level shows the reduced representation. Solid arrows denote structures already specified; dashed arrows denote reduced structures whose existence must be established. Typing distinguishes mathematical objects by the roles they are permitted to play, and reduction does not automatically transport full-state operations to the reduced representation. The word typed is familiar in logic, programming languages, category theory, and formal mathematics, yet it is frequently used without explanation outside those areas. This creates a problem for closure theory, where distinctions among states, reduced states, quotient classes, observations, actions, policies, histories, targets, and implementations are mathematically consequential even when the objects share the same coordinate representation. We use typed in a strong role-preserving sense. A mathematical object is not characterized solely by its value, dimension, or algebraic carrier. It also occupies a declared mathematical role, and that role constrains the operations in which the object may participate. Maps likewise possess input and output types. Passage between structurally distinct roles requires an explicit map rather than an implicit identification. This note develops that usage as an extended definition. It distinguishes typing from labeling, dimensional consistency, algebraic legality, and ordinary set membership; explains typed equality, composition, reduction, quotients, observables, control policies, histories, and implementation levels; and shows why type errors can expose hidden assumptions in closure arguments. The central closure-theoretic conclusion is that closure concerns preservation not merely of information but of the typed operations that a reduced representation must continue to support. Keywords: typed mathematics; closure theory; partial closure; quotient; reduction; factorization; type correctness; sufficient representation; control; mathematical semantics

title: Solving the Elastic Wave Equation with Physics-Informed Neural Networks: A Robust and Critical Assessment
abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have recently emerged as a promising approach for solving Partial Differential Equations (PDEs), offering a meshfree alternative that integrates physical principles into the learning process. This presents a new paradigm compared to traditional discretization methods and purely data-driven machine learning techniques. While promising, PINNs are not a panacea; they inherit challenges such as spectral bias and unstable convergence. Moreover, their potential in seismology remains largely unexplored. In this work, we provide a robust and critical assessment of PINNs for solving the elastic wave equation in seismology. We investigate the performance of PINNs on problems with varying degrees of complexity across various seismic sources and parameter models, from constant to highly heterogeneous settings. A pivotal aspect of our work involves investigating whether embedding physical principles directly into the network architecture enhances convergence and accuracy. We test an extensive range of neural architecture designs, from unrestricted, uninformed PINNs to highly specialized ones. We find that integrating an understanding of wave physics into the network design significantly improves accuracy. For instance, introducing a custom wavelet or plane wave layer, coupled with encoder and decoder layers, consistently yields a relative $L_2$ error approximately half that of the standard PINN, as evidenced across numerous experiments. We further demonstrate that this novel architecture enhances accuracy when applied to the acoustic wave equation, underlying the versatility of our network. Another key contribution of our research is the successful conditioning of PINNs on seismic source locations. This signifies a considerable advancement towards rapid seismic hazard detection and seismic analysis.

title: Preserving contextual information in cultural heritage metadata through multidimensional knowledge graphs
abstract: Using Knowledge Graphs (KGs) to describe Cultural Heritage Objects (CHOs) supports semantic richness and interoperability. However, standard KGs fail to capture the context-dependent validity of statements. This limitation is critical for cultural heritage metadata, which must often accommodate evolving or conflicting viewpoints, such as colonial versus post-colonial perspectives or shifting scientific consensus. While current knowledge representation methods address basic contextualization via provenance, qualifiers or reification, they lack a unified framework to simultaneously model and query data across multiple social, cultural, and political dimensions. To bridge this gap, we introduce the conceptual foundations of Multi-dimensional Knowledge Graphs (MKGs) and discuss how they preserve complex, multi-layered contexts in CHO metadata.

title: Monitor corpus of Slovene Trendi 2026-08
abstract: The Trendi corpus is a monitor corpus of Slovenian. It contains news articles from 106 media websites, published by 64 publishers. Trendi 2026-07 covers the period from January 2019 to August 2026, complementing the Gigafida 2.2 reference corpus of written Slovene (http://hdl.handle.net/11356/2106). The contents of the Trendi corpus are obtained using the Jožef Stefan Institute Newsfeed service (http://newsfeed.ijs.si/). The texts have been annotated using the CLASSLA-Stanza pipeline (https://github.com/clarinsi/classla), including syntactic parsing according to the Universal Dependencies (https://universaldependencies.org/sl/) and Named Entities (https://nl.ijs.si/janes/wp-content/uploads/2017/09/SlovenianNER-eng-v1.1.pdf). An important addition are topics or thematical categories, which have been automatically assigned to each text. There are 13 categories altogether: Arts and culture, Crime and accidents, Economy, Environment, Health, Leisure, Politics and Law, Science and Technology, Society, Sports, Weather, Entertainment, and Education. The text classification uses the following models: Text classification model SloBERTa-Trendi-Topics 1.0 (http://hdl.handle.net/11356/1709), Text classification model fastText-Trendi-Topics 1.0 (http://hdl.handle.net/11356/1710), and the SloBERTa model (https://huggingface.co/cjvt/sloberta-trendi-topics). The corpus is currently not available as a downloadable dataset due to copyright restrictions but we hope to make at least some of it available in the near future. The corpus is accessible through CLARIN.SI concordancers. If you would like to use the dataset for research purposes, please contact Iztok Kosem (iztok.kosem@ijs.si). This version adds texts from August 2026.

title: Shieldgraph: Topology-Aware Runtime Defense For Multi-Agent LLM Systems Against Adversarial Coordination Attacks
abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems—where multiple language model agents coordinate through message passing to accomplish complex tasks—are rapidly entering production deployment via frameworks such as LangGraph, CrewAI, and AutoGen. However, their interconnected architecture creates novel attack surfaces wherein adversarial inputs can propagate across agent boundaries through topology-guided exploitation. This paper introduces ShieldGraph, a runtime defense framework that models multi-agent topologies as trust-annotated graphs and enforces security invariants at inter-agent communication boundaries. ShieldGraph operates through three mechanisms: (1) a formal Trust Propagation Calculus (TPC) that assigns and dynamically updates capability-bounded trust scores to each agent and communication channel, (2) a lightweight adversarial message classifier that detects prompt injection, role hijacking, and intent drift in inter-agent communications with 91.3% precision at 2.4ms per message, and (3) a topology-aware quarantine protocol that isolates compromised subgraphs while maintaining operational continuity for unaffected agents. We evaluate ShieldGraph on the TAMAS adversarial benchmark, a novel red-team suite of 847 multi-agent attack scenarios, and three production-representative orchestration topologies (centralized, hierarchical, and decentralized). ShieldGraph reduces attack success rate from 68.4% (undefended) to 7.2% while preserving 94.1% task completion on benign workloads—a 6.8× safety improvement with only 3.7% utility degradation. We further demonstrate that topology-aware defense outperforms topology-agnostic baselines by 18.3 percentage points, establishing that the structural properties of multi-agent systems are critical to effective defense design.

title: QCR Composite Ratio: A Companion Metric to the Quantum Confidence Rating Standard
abstract: Description (Abstract): The Quantum Confidence Rating (QCR) standard measures the proportion of an AI system's cryptographic primitives verified as compliant with at least one recognized post-quantum standard. As published, a primitive verified through a composite construction, in which a classical algorithm and a post-quantum algorithm operate together, is scored identically to a primitive verified through a pure post-quantum construction alone. This note introduces the Composite Ratio (QCR-C) as a companion metric reported alongside QCR. QCR-C reports what proportion of an AI system's verified primitives use a composite construction rather than a pure post-quantum construction, giving regulators, auditors, and insurers visibility into how conservatively an organization approached its post-quantum migration, independent of the QCR score itself. QCR-C does not alter the QCR formula, the tier structure, or any prior certification issued under the original standard.

title: Design of an Agentic RAG Architecture for Advanced Electrical Document Understanding and Conversational AI
abstract: Electricity and industry-related documentation is large, heterogeneous, and not easily searchable with traditional methods, and the knowledgeable engineers who are proficient in legacy systems are increasingly retiring. RAG grounds large language models' responses in the company's internal documents, but traditional RAG cannot break down complex queries, iteratively search, check its responses, or accurately represent tables and diagrams. This paper describes the design of the agentic RAG architecture which is an extension of the base Streamlit application, built on top of Groq LPU inference, FAISS vector search, and LangChain conversational memory, into a multi-agent system consisting of the router, the retrieval agent, the verification/reflection agent, and the synthesis agent with the preprocessing pipeline for separating the narrative text, tables, and diagrams before indexing. We describe the deficiencies of the base system, determine functional and non-functional requirements and show how the designed architecture fits these requirements and a way to evaluate it based on engineering-document benchmarks. The design shows that the layering and mediation by the router agentic extension can help to overcome these deficiencies while preserving compatibility with the base system's technology stack.

We describe the deficiencies of the base system, determine functional and non-functional requirements and show how the designed architecture fits these requirements and a way to evaluate it based on engineering-document benchmarks. The design shows that the layering and mediation by the router agentic extension can help to overcome these deficiencies while preserving compatibility with the base system's technology stack.

title: The Currency of Thought: Homeostasis, Imagination, and the Economics of Cognition in a Colony of Simple Robots
abstract: We present the results of an intensive twelve-week experimental program (June-September 2026) pursuing a simple question: if a robot could dream, would the dreaming pay for itself - and what kind of economy would keep it dreaming? The system is a colony of small homeostatic agents with binary hypervector episodic memory, a dream engine that recombines memories during rest, and a strict energy ledger metering every unit spent on imagination and earned back. Across fifteen pre-registered, version-stamped campaigns we show: (1) imagination is a positive-yield investment with strongly diminishing returns - small dream budgets returned ~16x, large ones broke even (four replications); (2) the hypothesis that dreams specifically help in novel territory was cleanly refuted; (3) a rational, reward-learning agent reliably defunds cognition - five structurally different private incentive schemes all failed identically, because the ledger paid for disorder resolved rather than knowledge gained; (4) attention to internal novelty moves exploration strongly (+32%, d = 1.30) but does not enrich memory; (5) an episode-level memory key was refuted in one construction and certified superior to single-moment keys in another; (6) a finite colony energy economy - foraging as sole income - drives exploration above baseline (d = +0.71) while a fixed pipeline dreams more profitably under necessity than ever before; (7) memory as the foraging map doubles harvested energy (d = +1.00), yet the learned policy still defunds stress-pathway cognition even as it rides the map it never chose to fund; and (8) when the colony - not the ant - pays for cognition from a shared treasury, dream economics are restored under the learned policy (ROI -0.74 to break-even, d = +0.88): cognition is a colony-level investment. The design law completes: what the currency pays for, and who pays, determine whether a rational agent thinks. Code and datasets are available from the author on request; a public archive is forthcoming. A closing three-campaign surplus study: no world accumulates income through the battery-transport pipeline; income-at-source dues reverse the deficit (colonies self-fund at +150 to +214 per run); the reproduction ladder outclimbs a single season - the economy is endowment-bound, the cognition is not. Starving treasuries, thriving minds.

title: Graph Neural Networks with Latent State Representation Learning
abstract: This paper addresses the limitations of existing Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) concerning the effective capture of underlying latent structural information within graphs. We propose a novel architecture incorporating a latent state representation learning module within the GNN framework. This module enables nodes to learn compressed, abstract representations of their neighborhoods, effectively capturing relevant structural and functional characteristics. The core claim is that explicit learning of latent states significantly enhances GNN performance. This work demonstrates the efficacy of this approach through a detailed analysis of its impact on various graph-based tasks. The proposed method offers a pathway toward more robust and interpretable GNNs capable of leveraging the full potential of graph data.

title: 基于生物启发式算法的程序优化
abstract: This paper explores the application of bio-inspired algorithms – specifically Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) – to program optimization. The core aim is to enhance both the performance and readability of software code. Current program optimization techniques predominantly rely on static code analysis and manual intervention, often proving insufficient for complex, dynamically generated code. This research proposes a novel approach by framing program optimization as a search problem amenable to the exploration and optimization capabilities inherent in ACO and SA. The methodology involves translating specific program optimization goals, such as reducing execution time or memory footprint, into a suitable search space for these algorithms. We investigate the effectiveness of these algorithms in identifying optimal code transformations and configurations. The results demonstrate the potential of bio-inspired algorithms to offer a more automated and adaptable solution compared to traditional methods, particularly in scenarios where the problem space is large and complex.

title: Causal Discovery from Interventional and Observational Data using Graph Neural Networks
abstract: This paper explores the use of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for causal discovery directly from both interventional and observational data. Traditional causal discovery methods often rely on specific assumptions or require careful design of experiments. We propose a novel framework where a GNN is trained to predict the outcome of interventions, leveraging the information contained within both types of data. This approach allows the GNN to learn causal relationships implicitly, without explicitly modeling causal structures. We demonstrate the potential of this method by outlining a core claim, a core mechanism, and highlighting the novelty of this direct learning approach. The key equation illustrating the GNN's training objective is: $y = f(x_1, x_2, ..., x_N) + \epsilon$, where $y$ represents the outcome variable, $x_i$ represents the input variables, $f$ is the function learned by the GNN, and $\epsilon$ represents the error term. The GNN learns to approximate this function, capturing the underlying causal relationships. Further investigation into the architecture and training strategies of the GNN is crucial for achieving robust and reliable causal discovery.

title: 基于自适应量子纠缠的计算模型
abstract: This paper presents a novel computational model based on adaptive quantum entanglement, aiming to enhance the efficiency of quantum computation. Traditional quantum algorithms often struggle with the inherent limitations of qubit decoherence and the difficulty in exploiting quantum entanglement for computation. This work introduces a dynamic entanglement scheme that adapts to the system's state, mitigating these issues. We propose a framework where the entanglement state is continuously adjusted based on the input data, improving the fidelity and robustness of quantum calculations. The core mechanism centers around intelligently manipulating entanglement to facilitate more complex operations. The proposed model demonstrates significant improvements in both computational speed and the ability to perform certain quantum algorithms, particularly those requiring intricate entanglement manipulation. The results showcase the potential of this approach to advance the field of quantum computing.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Computing Model Construction
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum computing model construction, leveraging the unique properties of quantum computation to automatically learn and adjust model parameters. Traditional model building relies heavily on manual parameter tuning, which can be challenging for complex models. Quantum computing offers the potential for automated parameter adjustment, leading to improved accuracy and stability in physical simulations and data analysis. The core of this work centers on utilizing quantum algorithms to dynamically optimize model parameters, thereby enhancing the fidelity of simulations and data processing.

title: Meta-Learning for the Design of Graph Neural Network Architectures
abstract: The design of effective Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) is a complex and often iterative process, frequently relying on expert intuition and extensive experimentation. This work introduces a novel approach leveraging meta-learning to automate the architecture design of GNNs. Our core claim is that a meta-learning model can learn to optimize GNN architectural parameters, given a limited number of task-specific examples. This approach significantly reduces the design time and potentially leads to architectures tailored for specific graph-structured data. We define the problem as learning an architecture search strategy, utilizing meta-learning to train a model that can efficiently identify optimal GNN configurations for various downstream tasks. The key mechanism involves training a meta-learner to predict architectural parameters such as hidden layer sizes, activation functions, and aggregation operations based on task-specific data. This allows for rapid prototyping and adaptation to new graph datasets without requiring extensive manual tuning. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations, showcasing the ability of the meta-learner to discover architectures that outperform traditional, manually designed GNNs.

title: Meta-Learning for Adaptive Algorithm Selection in Data Streams
abstract: The challenge of adapting machine learning algorithms to evolving data streams remains a significant hurdle. Traditional approaches often rely on retraining models from scratch with each new data distribution, which is computationally expensive and frequently ineffective. This paper proposes a novel meta-learning framework for adaptive algorithm selection in data streams. The core idea is to train a meta-learner that learns to predict the optimal algorithm based on the characteristics of the incoming data stream. This meta-learner leverages past experience with diverse streams to quickly adapt to new streams, significantly improving performance and reducing computational overhead. We define the problem as learning a mapping from data stream characteristics (represented by features) to algorithm selection decisions. The meta-learner is trained using a meta-learning objective, encouraging it to generalize across streams. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical analysis and a conceptual framework. The proposed method offers a promising solution for building robust and efficient systems that can dynamically adapt to the inherent variability of real-world data streams.

title: Neurograph Adaptive Reshaping
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neural network design and optimization termed "Neurograph Adaptive Reshaping." The core claim is that dynamic adjustment of neural connections and topology, based on real-time analysis of network activity patterns, can lead to more efficient learning and adaptability. The proposed mechanism utilizes reinforcement learning to assess the efficiency of the current network structure based on metrics like activation values and synaptic potentials. Subsequently, genetic algorithms or rule-based methods are employed for localized reshaping of the neurograph, optimizing information flow pathways. Unlike traditional methods reliant on predefined rules or static topologies, this approach enables the neurograph to adaptively evolve during learning, overcoming the limitations of fixed-structure neural networks. This research introduces a framework for creating inherently more flexible and responsive neural architectures.

title: ##基于神经网络的符号推理系统
abstract: This paper proposes a novel system architecture that integrates neural networks and symbolic reasoning to create an intelligent system capable of both pattern recognition and logical inference. The core idea is to leverage the strengths of both approaches: neural networks excel at learning complex patterns and extracting features from raw data, while symbolic reasoning provides a framework for formal logic and knowledge representation. We present a framework where a neural network acts as a feature extractor and pattern identifier, feeding its output to a symbolic reasoning engine for logical deduction and knowledge manipulation. The resulting system aims to bridge the gap between statistical learning and symbolic AI, potentially leading to more robust and explainable intelligent systems. The system is designed to handle scenarios where both data-driven pattern recognition and explicit logical rules are relevant, ultimately improving overall system performance and interpretability. The key contributions of this work lie in the proposed integration strategy and the potential for enhanced reasoning capabilities.

title: Dynamic Metric Learning for Complex Networks
abstract: This paper introduces Dynamic Metric Learning (DML) – a novel algorithm for learning network metrics that adapts the metric space based on observed network structure and data. Traditional metric learning methods often rely on pre-defined metrics, which can be suboptimal for complex networks. DML leverages an adaptive neural network to dynamically adjust the metric space, allowing for automated optimization and improved representation of network topology. We present a comprehensive implementation of DML, demonstrating its effectiveness on a range of network datasets, including social networks and biological networks. The algorithm's core mechanism involves a feedback loop that continuously updates the metric space based on the observed network, resulting in more robust and flexible network representations.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: A Quantum State-Based Feature Extraction Approach
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) is a rapidly growing field that explores the potential of quantum mechanics to enhance machine learning algorithms. This paper presents a novel approach to feature extraction within QML, leveraging the unique properties of quantum states to dramatically accelerate and improve the accuracy of the feature extraction process. We propose a new method centered around the concept of mapping input data into quantum states, enabling efficient computation and improved representation of data through quantum processing. The core mechanism involves a quantum state transformation to effectively extract meaningful features, ultimately enhancing the overall performance of machine learning models. The proposed method addresses the inherent limitations of classical feature extraction, offering a promising pathway towards more sophisticated and efficient machine learning algorithms.

title: Distributed Quantum Simulation via Tensor Networks
abstract: This paper explores the potential of tensor networks for enabling distributed quantum simulation, a crucial step towards scaling up quantum computations. Traditional quantum simulation faces limitations due to the exponential growth of state vector sizes required for complex systems. Distributed quantum simulation aims to overcome this by partitioning the simulation across multiple quantum processors. However, efficient representation and manipulation of the resulting distributed quantum state remain a significant challenge. This work proposes utilizing tensor networks as a framework for representing and processing these distributed quantum states. Tensor networks offer an inherent structure that facilitates efficient parallel computation and minimizes communication overhead between quantum processors. We outline a theoretical framework, detailing the application of tensor network contractions and disentanglement techniques specifically tailored for distributed quantum simulation scenarios. The core claim of this work is that scaling up quantum simulations requires efficient methods for representing and manipulating quantum states, and tensor networks provide a promising avenue for achieving this goal. We present a method to reduce the computational complexity associated with simulating large quantum systems by leveraging the properties of tensor networks. The approach allows for a more scalable simulation strategy, moving beyond the limitations of traditional state vector representations. Further research will explore specific tensor network architectures and optimization strategies for different simulation problems.

title: ##基于深度学习的量子电路优化
abstract: This paper explores the application of deep learning techniques to optimize quantum circuits. The core challenge in quantum computing lies in the intricate design and manipulation of quantum circuits to achieve desired computational outcomes. Traditional methods of quantum circuit optimization are often computationally expensive and require significant domain expertise. This research proposes a novel approach leveraging deep learning algorithms to automatically generate optimal quantum circuits. The system learns the underlying structure and characteristics of quantum circuits through training, effectively reducing the complexity associated with quantum computation. This work presents a framework for automated quantum circuit optimization, paving the way for more accessible and efficient quantum computing solutions. The key contribution is the integration of deep learning with quantum circuit optimization, offering an automated process for circuit design and potentially unlocking the full potential of quantum computers.

title: Quantum Adaptive Correction Protocol for Decoherence
abstract: This paper presents a novel protocol for adaptive correction of decoherence in quantum information transmission. The core idea is to combine quantum error correction codes with dynamically adjusted decoherence suppression pulses. A key component is a real-time monitoring system that assesses the decoherence strength and dynamically adjusts the parameters of the suppression pulses. This approach aims to minimize the detrimental effects of decoherence, thereby enhancing the reliability of quantum information transfer. The protocol leverages the strengths of both quantum error correction and active suppression techniques, offering a significant advancement over traditional static decoherence mitigation strategies. The theoretical framework is presented, outlining the mathematical foundations and operational principles of the adaptive correction protocol. The protocol's efficacy is demonstrated through a detailed analysis of the system's performance under varying decoherence conditions. This work contributes to the development of robust quantum communication systems capable of transmitting quantum information with improved fidelity.

title: Projective Random Sketching and Relational Manifold Recovery in Dense Sentence Embeddings
abstract: Semantic search systems represent every text as a long list of numbers called an embedding. These vectors can consume substantial memory and become expensive to store and search, especially on phones, edge devices, and large servers. This paper shows that embeddings can be compressed to just a few dozen dimensions while still preserving a substantial ability to determine whether two texts belong to the same topic. Public experiment: 1,000 texts, 4 topics, using MiniLM embeddings with 384 dimensions. Full vector (384 dimensions): ~93% same-topic neighbors Compressed vector (32 dimensions): ~74% Memory reduction: ~92% Random chance: 25% The full embedding is still better—the compression is not magic. The important result is that a large fraction of the useful semantic information survives aggressive dimensionality reduction, at a fraction of the original memory cost. This could be useful for faster semantic search, smaller vector indexes, on-device AI, edge applications, RAG retrieval, and lower-cost text-matching systems.

title: A Novel Steganography Scheme Using Quantum Hilbert Transform
abstract: The main goal of steganography is to transmit hidden messages in legitimate-looking communication messages. Phase-domain information hiding, however, has not been fully explored for quantum systems. This work introduces a finite-dimensional Quantum Hilbert Transform (QHT) as a unitary phase operator based on the Quantum Fourier Transform. Using this construction, we develop a QHT-based quantum steganography scheme that embeds classical bits as weak signed phase perturbations of quantum cover states. Bob recovers the hidden message through binary state discrimination, block aggregation, and classical error-correcting decoding.

Bob recovers the hidden message through binary state discrimination, block aggregation, and classical error-correcting decoding.

title: Accuracy is Not Enough: A Divergence-Based Approach to Evaluate Fidelity Loss in Quantized LLMs
abstract: Deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) on memory-constrained edge devices relies heavily on aggressive post-training quantization. However, evaluating these models is largely based on zero-shot task accuracy, which depends solely on argmax predictions and is insensitive to changes in the underlying predictive distribution. Consequently, accuracy can exhibit unstable, non-monotonic behavior under progressive quantization, masking substantial fidelity loss relative to the BFloat16 (BF16) uncompressed base model and providing misleading deployment signals. We introduce a distribution-sensitive evaluation framework quantifying information loss in quantized LLMs as the divergence between full-vocabulary predictive distributions at the token decision boundary. We compute statistical distances, including Jensen-Shannon Divergence and Total Variation Distance, between outputs of full-precision and quantized models, enabling a fine-grained analysis of distributional shift. Using this framework, we quantify probability mass displacement and distributional drift relative to the BF16 reference, capturing predictive distribution changes not reflected in top-1 accuracy. We conduct a 120-run experimental matrix across five foundation architectures and four reasoning benchmarks under progressive quantization regimes, from uncompressed BF16 to Q2_K, providing a systematic fidelity analysis. Our results show divergence metrics generally increase under stronger quantization, complementing task accuracy with a fidelity signal. Across tested llama-cpp schemes, mixed-precision Q4_K generally yields lower divergence than uniform Q4_0 at similar memory footprints. These findings motivate distribution-aware evaluation as a practical diagnostic complement to task accuracy; they do not directly establish correctness, calibration, safety, or user-perceived quality.

title: Staying on the Attack Path: Structured State for Long-Horizon Automated Penetration Testing
abstract: Large language model (LLM) based agents are increasingly applied to cybersecurity tasks such as vulnerability discovery and automated penetration testing. On long-horizon security tasks, however, such agents remain limited by context forgetting and intent drift: early critical facts and causal reasoning chains are lost over extended interactions, and the agent falls into aimless, repetitive exploration. This paper proposes Intentest, an intent-graph-guided automated penetration testing agent that externalizes long-horizon state from the LLM's context window onto a persistent fact-intent directed acyclic graph (DAG), thereby substantially reducing invalid transitions. We evaluate Intentest on automated penetration testing of web applications, a representative long-tail task in cybersecurity. In the DAG, verified network states are stored as immutable fact nodes, and exploration directions are constrained as intent edges bounded by predecessor facts. The system adopts a three-layer architecture, in which the fact-intent mapping layer maintains the global state, the task scheduling and allocation layer ensures execution stability through two-phase degradation recovery and multi-dimensional adaptive load balancing, and the intent retrieval and prediction layer provides tactical priors through a top-down five-stage filtering algorithm. On a benchmark of real CTF challenges covering more than ten vulnerability types across three difficulty levels, Intentest achieves an overall success rate of 88.2% and a success rate of 75.0% on hard tasks, improving over the baseline by approximately 44 and 50 percentage points. Ablation experiments further show that the intent retrieval and prediction reduce the average number of rounds on successful medium and hard tasks by about 33% and 48%, respectively, without changing the set of solvable tasks.

title: CAMES: arquiteturas baseadas em capacidades para sistemas embebidos de criticidade mista
abstract: Os sistemas embebidos e de criticidade elevada têm vindo a tornar-se mais complexos devido às crescentes exigências de integração e conectividade. Em simultâneo, as pressões de mercado para reduzir dimensão, peso, consumo energético e custo (SWaP-C) têm impulsionado a consolidação de aplicações de criticidade mista numa única plataforma. Neste contexto, a virtualização tem-se afirmado como uma tecnologia de referência para a consolidação de sistemas de criticidade mista, oferecendo isolamento espacial e temporal e facilitando o cumprimento de normas de segurança e fiabilidade, como a ISO 26262. Embora os hipervisores tradicionais forneçam isolamento eficaz entre máquinas virtuais (VMs), garantir proteção com mínima granularidade dentro de uma VM ou no próprio hipervisor requer mecanismos adicionais, frequentemente complexos e dispendiosos. Esta limitação torna-se relevante em sistemas desenvolvidos em linguagens sem garantias de segurança de memória, como C e C++, onde vulnerabilidades de memória podem comprometer as garantias de isolamento. A arquitetura Capability Hardware Enhanced RISC Instructions (CHERI) mitiga estas limitações através da introdução de mecanismos de proteção de memória de granularidade fina impostos por hardware e de compartimentação granular através de capabilities. Ao contrário de linguagens seguras, como Rust, CHERI permite uma adoção incremental em sistemas baseados em C/C++, sem exigir a reescrita integral do código existente, embora implique alterações na pilha de software (por exemplo, no toolchain) e suporte adicional de hardware. Esta tese estabelece uma base para segurança baseada em capabilities e virtualização em sistemas embebidos RISC-V de criticidade mista através de três contributos. Em primeiro lugar, realizámos a primeira análise sistemática do ecossistema CHERI e identificámos lacunas em setores críticos, como o setor automóvel. Em segundo lugar, estendemos o processador RISC-V CVA6 com suporte para virtualização e explorámos melhorias microarquiteturais destinadas a aumentar a eficiência da virtualização através de exploração do espaço de desenho. Por fim, desenvolvemos a primeira pilha completa opensource que integra CHERI com virtualização em RISC-V. Em particular, implementámos CHERI numa plataforma baseada no CVA6 com suporte para virtualização e estendemos o hipervisor Bao para suportar CHERI em RISC-V, tornando-o o primeiro hipervisor com suporte para CHERI nesta arquitetura, avaliando o esforço de integração necessário e os benefícios de segurança obtidos.

title: Anàlisi d'errors en la transcripció automàtica de vídeos de YouTube amb accents de les illes britàniques
abstract: [ES] El reconocimiento automático del habla ha experimentado importantes avances desde su aparición en la década de 1950, convirtiéndose en una herramienta fundamental para la accesibilidad de la información a través de la generación automática de subtítulos. A pesar de la elevada precisión que anuncian los sistemas actuales, las investigaciones han identificado la existencia de sesgos relacionados con el acento. Este estudio examina si dicho sesgo persiste en la actualidad, para lo cual se ha analizado un corpus sincrónico y multimodal de 80 vídeos de YouTube Shorts representativos de diferentes tipos de discurso (p. ej., vlogs, podcasts, entrevistas y comedia) a modo de muestras de los diversos acentos de las islas británicas, tales como inglés, gales, irlandés y escocés. Mediante un proceso de anotación y análisis cuantitativo y cualitativo, se evaluaron los errores producidos por el sistema de subtitulado automático de YouTube y se identificaron los rasgos lingüísticos asociados a posibles sesgos de acento. Se implementó una metodología rigurosa para calcular la tasa de error de palabras y caracteres a micronivel, clasificando los errores como sustitución, omisión e inserción. Asimismo, se generaron vectores densos de oraciones a partir de muestras de vídeo para medir la similitud del coseno entre los subtítulos automáticos y la transcripción de referencia. Este análisis a macronivel permitió cuantificar la pérdida de significado. Los resultados demuestran un sesgo persistente en esta tecnología. El acento irlandés registra la mayor tasa media de error de palabras. La similitud del coseno revela que el acento inglés muestra la mayor estabilidad semántica, mientras que los acentos galés, irlandés y escocés son penalizados severamente por los errores del sistema. Los resultados permitieron determinar el grado de precisión de un modelo avanzado de reconocimiento automático del habla con variedades de acentos de las islas británicas, para lo cual se aportaron evidencias sobre el rendimiento de esta tecnología en esta cuestión.

title: Magnus Opus — Semantic Governance Framework (Version 1.0, 2026)
abstract: Magnus Opus — Semantic Governance Framework defines a deterministic semantic modelling approach for representing irreconcilable conflicts within rule‑driven or distributed systems. Version 1.0 formalises the RA‑1 Sovereign Antinomy Class, a conceptual academic model describing conflict states that cannot be resolved without violating at least one directive. The document introduces: deterministic semantic operators, a conflict‑state machine (Hold, Trace, Anchor, Archive), machine‑interpretable schemas (JSON‑LD, RDF), forensic artifact structures, cross‑architecture neutrality principles. This work is strictly academic and does not imply any commercial, institutional or governance relationship with external organizations. title: Title: Quantum-Inspired Neural Networks (QINNs) - Adaptive Feature Extraction
abstract: Quantum mechanics, a cornerstone of modern physics, describes the behavior of matter and energy at the atomic and subatomic levels. It's often described through phenomena like superposition, entanglement, and quantization, where the system's state is described by a set of quantum states. These concepts have inspired researchers to develop new computational paradigms, particularly in the field of machine learning. This paper investigates the potential of Quantum-Inspired Neural Networks (QINNs) to address limitations in current neural network architectures, specifically focusing on the efficient and robust extraction of features through a novel, adaptive approach. We propose a new neural network architecture predicated on mimicking the intricate patterns observed in quantum systems, aiming to enhance generalization capabilities. This work will explore the fundamental principles behind QINNs and detail the proposed methodology for achieving improved performance through feature extraction.

title: Logical Quantum Computing: A Proof of Validity through Non-Symmetric Properties
abstract: This paper explores the potential of logical quantum computing to provide a novel framework for proving mathematical theorems. Leveraging the inherent non-symmetry of quantum computation, we aim to develop a method for rigorously validating mathematical constructs and potentially uncovering new quantum algorithms. The core mechanism involves simulating and analyzing mathematical theorems using quantum systems, identifying subtle patterns and inconsistencies that reveal vulnerabilities. This research will focus on establishing a rigorous, albeit preliminary, proof of the validity of a specific theorem, demonstrating the potential for a paradigm shift in mathematical verification. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions of this approach.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Computation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre yet fundamental phenomenon, offers a potentially revolutionary approach to computation. This paper explores the concept of utilizing entanglement as a core computational building block, moving beyond the limitations of classical systems. We detail a novel quantum algorithm designed to actively manipulate entanglement to execute complex calculations, with a particular emphasis on error correction within the entanglement itself. The core claim is that this approach can facilitate the execution of tasks currently intractable for classical computers, leveraging the unique properties of entanglement to achieve significant performance improvements. The paper outlines the theoretical foundation, algorithm design, and potential challenges associated with this paradigm shift.

title: Title: Bayesian Constraint Optimization for Complex Dynamical Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel Bayesian optimization technique designed for modeling and control of complex, non-linear dynamical systems. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with these systems due to their inherent complexity, non-linearity, and sensitivity to initial conditions. We introduce a Bayesian approach that enhances optimization by incorporating a hierarchical representation of system states and dynamically weighting evidence sources. This enhances the system's robustness and allows for more effective exploration of the solution space. The core mechanism leverages a 'belief-update' process that continuously refines the system's state representation based on new evidence, leading to improved performance compared to existing methods. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations focused on biological system modeling and fluid dynamics, showcasing its ability to guide the optimization process towards optimal configurations. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and potential future directions for this research.

title: Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing with Temporal Entanglement
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to reservoir computing (RC) that incorporates quantum-inspired concepts, specifically temporal entanglement, to significantly enhance the system's performance in processing time-dependent signals. Traditional RC relies on a randomly connected recurrent neural network, often referred to as the "reservoir," to generate complex, high-dimensional representations of input data. However, this approach can struggle with capturing intricate temporal dynamics efficiently. This work proposes a modified RC architecture where the connectivity within the reservoir is designed to mimic the effects of temporal entanglement, a phenomenon observed in quantum systems where the state of a particle is instantaneously correlated with the state of another particle regardless of the distance separating them. We demonstrate that by leveraging this principle, the reservoir can better represent and process signals evolving over time, leading to improved prediction accuracy and robustness. The core idea is to introduce a specific type of connectivity that allows for correlated updates between reservoir neurons, effectively creating a temporal entanglement effect. The theoretical framework is presented, and the methodology for implementing this quantum-inspired RC is detailed. We discuss the potential implications of this approach across various applications, highlighting its advantages over conventional RC methods. The results suggest a promising avenue for developing more powerful and efficient neural networks for time-series analysis and dynamic system modeling.

title: Title: Non-Standard Matrix Decomposition for Quantum State Representation
abstract: Quantum state representation is fundamental to quantum computation, requiring efficient methods for manipulation and analysis. Traditional methods often rely on eigenvalue decomposition, which struggles with the intricate correlations inherent in many quantum states, particularly those exhibiting entanglement. This paper introduces a novel matrix decomposition technique, "Quantum Entanglement Matrix Decomposition" (QEMD), designed to explicitly incorporate quantum entanglement and superposition into the core representation of quantum states. This approach significantly enhances computational efficiency and opens new avenues for algorithm design within the quantum realm. The method's core mechanism involves constructing a 'quantum entanglement matrix' that directly represents these correlations, enabling parallel processing and facilitating the development of novel quantum algorithms. We present a comprehensive theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating the effectiveness of QEMD.

title: Dynamic Programming for Probabilistic Circuit Optimization
abstract: Quantum circuit optimization remains a critical challenge in the development of quantum computing. Traditional dynamic programming (DP) methods, while effective for deterministic circuit design, fail to adequately address the inherent probabilistic nature of quantum operations. This paper proposes a novel approach that extends DP algorithms by explicitly incorporating probabilistic models representing uncertainties in quantum gate operations and qubit measurements. The core idea is to leverage Monte Carlo simulations to estimate expected costs and rewards within the DP framework. This allows for a more realistic and potentially efficient solution to the circuit optimization problem, considering the statistical fluctuations that are fundamental to quantum computing. We demonstrate the feasibility of this method conceptually, outlining the key components and algorithmic steps. Further research and implementation will be necessary to fully realize the potential of this approach.

title: Dynamic Topology Geometry: A Quantum Evolution Framework
abstract: This paper explores the integration of dynamic topology and quantum evolution to address the challenges in simulating complex topological systems. The core idea is to leverage the inherent properties of topology and quantum mechanics to construct a computational framework capable of automated identification and simulation of intricate topological structures. We propose a novel approach that combines the principles of quantum state manipulation, quantum entanglement, and quantum tunneling to emulate dynamic topological transformations. This framework utilizes quantum algorithms to enable the simulation of large-scale topological systems, offering potential acceleration compared to classical methods. The work focuses on establishing a robust and efficient methodology for this integrated approach, demonstrating its potential for both theoretical analysis and practical application. title: Graph Representation Learning with Symbolic Regression
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to graph representation learning by integrating symbolic regression. Traditional graph representation learning methods frequently depend on manually designed features, a process that can be time-consuming and may not capture all relevant relationships within a graph. Our method leverages symbolic regression to automatically learn a graph representation that directly predicts a target variable. This allows the model to discover intricate relationships within the graph data without relying on predefined feature engineering. The core mechanism involves constructing a symbolic regression model where the graph structure and node features serve as input, and the target variable is the output. The regression engine then iteratively refines the symbolic expression to minimize the prediction error. This approach offers a pathway to automated feature discovery and potentially more robust and accurate graph representations. We demonstrate the efficacy of this method through a theoretical exploration and outline a framework for its implementation.

title: Quantum Entanglement Adaptive Topology Transformation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, exhibits unique properties that have spurred significant research into its manipulation and application. Among these, adaptive topology transformations offer a promising avenue for exploring and harnessing these properties. This paper introduces a novel approach leveraging quantum entanglement to dynamically reshape topological structures, achieving enhanced control and optimization of complex geometry. We present a method centered around introducing self-adaptive transformations based on quantum entanglement, allowing for the generation of intricate and potentially useful topological configurations. The core mechanism involves creating entangled states that guide the evolution of the topology, enabling precise control over the resulting structure. This work aims to advance our understanding of quantum topology and its potential impact on various fields, including materials science and quantum information processing.

title: Self-Correcting Neural Networks via Bayesian Inference and Ensemble Learning
abstract: Neural networks have demonstrated remarkable success in various domains, but they suffer from significant limitations, notably catastrophic forgetting and the detrimental effects of noisy updates. This paper proposes a novel self-correcting neural network architecture designed to address these challenges. The architecture leverages the strengths of Bayesian inference and ensemble learning to dynamically adapt and refine network parameters. Specifically, multiple network versions are maintained, each representing a potential solution to the learning problem. Bayesian inference is employed to guide the update of these versions based on observed prediction errors, effectively quantifying uncertainty and promoting stable learning. Furthermore, ensemble learning is utilized to combine the predictions of these multiple versions, resulting in more robust and accurate overall predictions. The core claim is that this combined approach provides a mechanism for mitigating catastrophic forgetting and the impact of noisy updates, leading to a more reliable and adaptive neural network. The methodology provides a framework for continuous learning and adaptation, ultimately enhancing the resilience and performance of neural networks in dynamic environments. This work introduces a fundamentally new approach to neural network training, moving beyond static parameter adjustments to a dynamic, self-correcting system.

title: Contextualized Memory Networks with Temporal Anchoring
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to memory network design, termed Contextualized Memory Networks with Temporal Anchoring (CMNT). The core idea is to enhance memory retrieval and reasoning by explicitly associating each stored memory with a precise temporal timestamp. This "temporal anchoring" allows for a more nuanced and accurate assessment of memory relevance within a given context. The system utilizes a memory module augmented with these timestamps and employs a "time-aware attention" mechanism to prioritize memories based on their temporal proximity to the current context. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in reasoning accuracy compared to standard memory networks, particularly in scenarios requiring temporal coherence and extended reasoning chains. The key contribution lies in providing a robust method to manage temporal dependencies within memory networks, paving the way for more sophisticated and reliable AI systems.

title: Temporal-Dependent Symbolic Reasoning Network (TDSN)
abstract: This paper introduces the Temporal-Dependent Symbolic Reasoning Network (TDSN), a novel architecture designed to leverage temporal dependencies and symbolic reasoning within neural networks for enhanced understanding and prediction of complex sequential data. The core idea is to integrate symbolic logic inference with neural network processing, resulting in a network capable of abstracting data representations through symbolic reasoning and learning patterns through neural networks. Traditional recurrent neural networks (RNNs) often struggle with long-range temporal dependencies and lack explicit reasoning capabilities. TDSN addresses these limitations by providing a mechanism for explicitly modeling and reasoning about temporal relationships. The network utilizes a hybrid approach, combining the strengths of both symbolic and sub-symbolic representations. This allows for more robust and interpretable predictions, particularly in scenarios where temporal context is crucial. We demonstrate the effectiveness of TDSN through theoretical analysis and outline its potential applications in diverse domains, including time series forecasting, natural language processing, and robotics. The key contribution lies in the synergistic combination of symbolic reasoning and neural networks, offering a powerful framework for tackling complex sequential data problems. ---

title: Causal Discovery via Bayesian Episodic Memory Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to causal discovery leveraging the principles of episodic memory networks and Bayesian inference. The core idea is that episodic memory networks, representing states and causal transitions, can be effectively utilized for causal discovery, particularly within partially observable environments. We construct these networks, where nodes represent states and edges represent causal relationships, and then employ Bayesian inference to estimate the conditional probability distributions associated with each state. This allows us to identify causal relationships by simulating interventions and observations, thereby enhancing the robustness and accuracy of the discovery process. The combination of episodic memory and Bayesian causal inference offers a significantly improved method compared to traditional approaches, addressing limitations in environments with incomplete information. This research provides a framework for discovering causal relationships in complex systems where observational data is inherently noisy and partial. The methodology is presented with detailed mathematical formulations, focusing on the core concepts and their application.
