title: Probabilistic Programming with Adaptive Bayesian Model Selection
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to probabilistic programming that addresses the limitations of current systems regarding adaptive Bayesian model selection. The core claim is that existing probabilistic programming languages lack robust mechanisms for automatically adjusting model complexity. To address this, we propose a language feature enabling dynamic adaptation of Bayesian models through a meta-learning framework. This system intelligently selects the optimal model complexity based on observed data, improving computational efficiency and potentially enhancing predictive accuracy. We detail the proposed mechanism, highlighting its integration within the programming paradigm and emphasizing its potential for automated and intelligent model selection. The approach leverages the principles of Bayesian model selection, incorporating a dynamic adjustment strategy driven by a meta-learning process. The paper focuses on the theoretical foundations and design principles, outlining a framework for future implementation and exploration.

title: Dynamic distortion from discretized coupling feedback in soft-spin Ising machines
abstract: Although Ising machines (IMs) have grown in popularity due to their potential as physics-based accelerators for combinatorial optimization problems (COPs), most literature focuses on empirically-obtained benchmarks with low universality. In this work, we propose dynamic feedback distortion as a universal metric to quantify the effect of coupling field discretization in time-multiplexed IMs. Starting from the transfer functions of realistic hardware, we analytically show how this distortion can be mitigated using a global bias (or choosing the correct discrete coupling element) and injecting coloured noise. Our numerical results show that our mitigation protocols are very effective, especially in complicated energy landscapes (namely tunable Möbius ladders and 2D tiling problems); where an analogue reduction of the distortion leads to a two--three order of magnitude increase in the success rate of complex COPs.

title: CRISP: Corneal Confocal Microscopy Real-Time Image Stitching Pipeline
abstract: Morphology of the sub-basal nerve plexus (SNP) reflects peripheral nerve health, and corneal confocal microscopy (CCM) provides an important means for in vivo, real-time, non-invasive observation of the SNP. However, mainstream CCM devices offer a limited field of view per frame, whereas the SNP is spatially non-uniform; discrete image sampling is therefore sensitive to sampling location and frame selection, which limits the reproducibility and clinical adoption of CCM as a quantitative assessment tool. Wide-field stitching can reconstruct larger SNP mosaics by integrating sequentially acquired CCM images, but existing methods largely rely on offline post-processing, additional hardware, or specific acquisition protocols, and lack open-source real-time solutions for conventional CCM video streams. This paper presents CRISP (Corneal confocal microscopy Real-time Image Stitching Pipeline), an open-source real-time SNP wide-field stitching framework for conventional CCM examination video streams. CRISP excludes defocused and discontinuous segments via focus-aware gating, propagates poses through local pairwise registration, and maintains non-redundant spatial coverage with a sparse anchor map; when local temporal continuity is interrupted, the system completes relocalization and subgraph merging through global appearance retrieval followed by geometric verification. The framework prioritizes low-latency coverage feedback during examination while outputting accepted frames, poses, and anchor information to initialize offline fine stitching. To our knowledge, CRISP is the first open-source real-time SNP wide-field stitching framework released for conventional CCM video streams. By lowering the barrier to adoption and reproduction of wide-field stitching, CRISP may help move SNP wide-field imaging from a research tool into routine clinical examination workflows.

title: PhysSAE: Mechanistic Interpretability of PINNs with Sparse Autoencoders
abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) embed PDE residuals into neural network training, but their internal representations remain opaque: it is unknown what physical features their hidden layers encode or whether those features have a localized causal role. We present PhysSAE, a mechanistic interpretability framework that trains overcomplete sparse autoencoders (SAEs) on PINN penultimate-layer activations and evaluates dictionary atoms through direct causal intervention in the original frozen hidden state: $h_{\mathrm{cf}} = h - αz_k d_k$, bypassing the SAE decoder entirely. Across six PDE families, with 3 PINN seeds and 3 SAE seeds each---we show that (i) Our discovered SAE atoms align with independently-defined physical observables (max Pearson $|r|=0.951$, always $\gg$ permutation null), (ii) the causal footprint of top-aligned atom ablation is 1.2--4.2$\times$ more spatially concentrated canonical than PCA or ICA interventions, and (iii) top-aligned atoms outperform matched random controls on causal localization for structured physical concepts (ESF$_{80}$ advantage 0.04-0.44). Two-atom bilateral representations improve concept regression R$^2$ by $ΔR^2\!=\!0.05\text{-}0.15$ over single atoms, while random pairs decrease it by up to 0.60. These results demonstrate that PINNs develop sparse, physically structured latent representations that can be identified and causally interrogated post-hoc, opening a path toward interpretability-aware scientific machine learning.

title: Interpretabilitat en xarxes neuronals profundes: fonaments matemàtics i aplicació a la detecció de fractures de monyica
abstract: [ES] En los últimos años, la presencia de redes neuronales ha aumentado enormemente en aplicaciones de todo tipo. Gracias a su flexibilidad y escalabilidad, están siendo utilizadas en multitud de campos donde la inteligencia artificial resulta de gran utilidad. Sin embargo, en contraposición a muchos métodos clásicos de aprendizaje automático, las redes neuronales presentan un carácter de «caja negra» por el cual es muy difícil interpretar de qué forma la red ha tomado una decisión y qué características de la entrada han llevado a la red al estado final. El presente trabajo se encarga de abordar esta problemática y se centra en el área conocida como XAI (eXplaiable AI). Dado el carácter de «caja negra» que caracteriza a las redes neuronales profundas actuales, esta área está tomando cada vez más relevancia, pues conforme aumenta la complejidad y la presencia de los modelos en el día a día, se hace cada vez más complicado e importante entender de qué forma el modelo hace sus predicciones y cuando comete errores, determinar las causas. Este trabajo tiene dos propósitos y facetas: primeramente, el estudio teórico de algoritmos de explicabilidad así como sus fundamentos matemáticos, en el que se abordarán diferentes conceptos de teoría de juegos (SHAP), cálculo en varias variables (GRAD-CAM, Integrated Gradients) o teoría de aproximación y álgebra lineal (LIME), entre otros; y en segundo lugar, aplicar estas técnicas de interpretabilidad a un sector tan importante y crítico como lo es el análisis de imágenes médicas. Concretamente, se aplicará a la detección de fracturas de muñeca pediátricas utilizando el dataset GRAZPEDWRI-DX. Partiendo de un modelo basado en la arquitectura Faster-RCNN (evolución de la arquitectura clásica convolucional) capaz de detectar con precisión dichas fracturas, se aplicarán diferentes técnicas y algoritmos para discernir qué partes de la imagen son las que están condicionando al modelo y observar cómo «piensa» la red. Entre ellos destaca LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations), basado en generar datos artificiales a partir de pequeñas modificaciones de una muestra para observar qué características son las más relevantes para la salida de la red; GRAD-CAM (Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping), que evalúa el gradiente de la clasificación final respecto a las activaciones una capa convolucional para determinar qué neuronas han influido en mayor medida; o también SHAP, proveniente de los valores de Shapley de teoría de juegos, que se basan en dar una explicación aditiva, es decir, una explicación en la que cada característica suma un valor para llegar a la predicción final. Estos algoritmos tradicionalmente se aplican sobre clasificadores, es decir, modelos cuya respuesta es el escalar de la probabilidad de pertenecer a una clase determinada. Por ello, resulta interesante su aplicación y adaptación a arquitecturas de detección de objetos, pues se presentan diferentes alternativas para abordar el problema. Así, al aplicar estos algoritmos al mencionado dataset para ver de qué forma se pueden utilizar de forma práctica, se busca el evaluar el comportamiento de un modelo de red neuronal profunda de detección de objetos.

title: Reproduction package: How Chunk Size and Overlap Shape Retrieval-Augmented Generation — A Controlled Study of a Retrieval–Reading Tension
abstract: Code and pre-computed result files reproducing all tables and figures of the paper on the retrieval–reading tension in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) chunking. Includes one self-contained Python script per experiment (chunk-size/overlap/depth sweeps, dense-retrieval and generative-reader replications, sentence-boundary vs. fixed and modern-chunker comparisons, truncation and fixed-budget controls, supporting-fact recall, AutoChunk selection, and external validation on NewsQA), a README mapping scripts to paper elements, result CSVs, and pinned dependencies. All datasets are public (SQuAD, HotpotQA, DuoRC, NewsQA via Hugging Face). Runs on CPU with fixed seeds.

title: Operational Accessibility, State Economy, and the \delta^* Threshold Operator
abstract: Operational Accessibility, State Economy, and the \delta^* Threshold Operator CJ Tully Independent Researcher and Engineer ttg41postquantum@gmail.com chloetully5@gmail.com Date: 8th September 2026 Let an artificial cognitive or physical system at step t be described under a chosen representation space \mathcal{M} such that s_t = \pi(h_t) \in \mathcal{M}, where h_t \in \mathcal{H} represents the full historical trajectory of operations and observations. Rather than defining capability as an intrinsic vector of static functions assigned to an individuated agent, continuation is defined over an action space \mathcal{A} governed by an Admissibility Field \mathcal{F}_t = \{ a \in \mathcal{A} \mid \mathcal{C}(a \mid s_t, \mathcal{R}) \le \theta_{\text{adm}} \}, where \mathcal{R} denotes the local resource regime, \mathcal{C}: \mathcal{A} \times \mathcal{M} \times \mathcal{R} \to \mathbb{R}^+ maps an operation to its execution cost, and \theta_{\text{adm}} is the strict admissibility boundary. A realised operation a_t \in \mathcal{F}_t produces a state update not by appending an informational token into a static memory buffer, but by transforming the geometry of \mathcal{F}_{t+1}; the fundamental unit of analysis is strictly the induced transition \mathcal{F}_t \xrightarrow{a_t} \mathcal{F}_{t+1}. Latent operational differences do not require postulating hidden ontologies: two histories h^{(1)} and h^{(2)} are operationally dormant under \pi if \pi(h^{(1)}) = \pi(h^{(2)}) = s and \mathcal{F}(s; \theta) \equiv \mathcal{F}^{(1)} = \mathcal{F}^{(2)}. The retuning operator \delta^* : \theta_{\text{adm}} \mapsto \theta_{\text{adm}} + \Delta \theta^* acts directly on the admissibility threshold such that \mathcal{F}_{\delta^*}(s) = \{ a \in \mathcal{A} \mid \mathcal{C}_{\delta^*}(a \mid s, \mathcal{R}) \le \theta_{\text{adm}} + \Delta \theta^* \}, causing previously indistinguishable trajectories to diverge interventionally (\mathcal{F}_{\delta^*}(h^{(1)}) \neq \mathcal{F}_{\delta^*}(h^{(2)})) without requiring retrospective modifications to the classical historical store. Conversely, the adjoint unlearning operator \delta^{*\dagger} renders an active operational distinction unreachable across all subsequent admissible continuations via \lim_{\delta^{*\dagger}} \mathcal{F}(s \oplus \Delta) \to \mathcal{F}(s). To determine whether an accessibility architecture provides genuine structural compression over unconstrained state expansion \mathcal{M}' \supset \mathcal{M}, the representation cost is quantified as the tuple \mathfrak{C}_{\text{rep}}(\mathcal{S}) = \langle d_{\text{eff}}(\mathcal{S}), B(\mathcal{S}), N_{\text{sample}}(\epsilon) \rangle, spanning effective tangent dimension d_{\text{eff}} = \operatorname{dim}(\operatorname{span}\{ \nabla_a \mathcal{C}(a \mid s) \mid a \in \mathcal{F}_{\delta^*} \}), boundary bit-depth B(\mathcal{S}) = \mathbb{I}(H_{\le t} ; \mathcal{F}_{> t}), and sample identification complexity N_{\text{sample}}, establishing strict superiority if and only if \mathfrak{C}_{\text{rep}}(\mathcal{F}_{\delta^*}) < \mathfrak{C}_{\text{rep}}(\mathcal{M}') at matched predictive divergence D_{\text{KL}} \le \epsilon. This architecture is empirically bounded by three protocols: Protocol I (Interventional Residue) falsifies persistence if a transported residue fails the mapping \mathcal{T}_{A \to B}(\mathcal{F}_A) = \mathcal{F}_B across distinct carriers; Protocol II (Regime Transformation) verifies that shifts in \delta^* alter the topology of reachable continuations rather than single-step token likelihoods; and Protocol III (Monitoring Depth Falsification) enforces a mandatory kill-switch, rejecting the accessibility hypothesis in favor of a minimal Markovian baseline whenever extending historical depth K > K_0 fails to produce a statistically significant reduction in \mathfrak{C}_{\text{rep}} or predictive error on held-out tasks.

title: PhysGuard-FL: Reproducibility package for physics-aware Byzantine-robust federated learning in chemical process monitoring
abstract: Complete research compendium for PhysGuard-FL, a physics-aware Byzantine-robust federated-learning framework evaluated for chemical-process monitoring. The frozen benchmark uses six Tennessee Eastman Process operating modes, 20 federated clients, 20 communication rounds, five local steps, and 10 matched random seeds. The primary robustness benchmark comprises 70 runs across seven aggregation methods under model-replacement attacks with 30% Byzantine clients. The secondary benchmark comprises 40 runs across four shared aggregation methods under sign-flip attacks with 20% Byzantine clients. The archive preserves all 110 run-level experiment outputs, original summaries, Student-t 95% confidence intervals, paired t-tests, Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, Holm-adjusted p-values, seed-wise wins and ranks, cross-attack comparisons, figures, documentation, and executable statistical post-processing scripts. The package supports transparent statistical auditing and reproducibility of the quantitative results reported in the associated PhysGuard-FL study.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Propagation for Complex Scheduling
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum computing to optimize scheduling algorithms, specifically targeting complex, dynamic systems. Current scheduling methods often struggle with intricate constraints and evolving demands, leading to inefficient resource allocation and suboptimal performance. We propose a novel quantum-enhanced constraint propagation scheme, leveraging quantum algorithms to accelerate the search for optimal schedules. The core mechanism focuses on exploring the solution space more efficiently, potentially reducing computational complexity significantly. This research explores the potential of quantum computing to overcome limitations inherent in traditional scheduling techniques, offering a promising avenue for improved scheduling efficiency. The paper details the implementation of the proposed scheme, demonstrates preliminary results, and discusses future research directions.

title: Quantum Entanglement Computation: Adaptive Topology for Enhanced Robustness and Efficiency
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental resource in quantum computation, enabling tasks such as quantum teleportation and superposition. However, achieving reliable and efficient quantum computation is hampered by the susceptibility of entangled states to environmental noise. This paper explores the application of adaptive topology in quantum computation to mitigate these vulnerabilities. We propose a novel quantum computing framework that dynamically adjusts the topology of the quantum system to minimize noise, thereby enhancing the robustness and efficiency of entanglement calculations, particularly in the context of complex quantum states. The core mechanism leverages the inherent properties of topology to create a more resilient and controllable quantum system. This research presents a new approach to quantum entanglement computation that promises significant advancements in the field.

title: 基于动态自适应的概率模型优化算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel probabilistic model optimization algorithm, termed the Dynamic Adaptive Probability Model Optimization Algorithm (DAPO). The algorithm addresses the limitations of traditional optimization methods by incorporating a dynamic probability field mechanism that adapts to data feedback and model error. The core innovation lies in the ability of DAPO to dynamically adjust probability parameters, leading to significantly improved model prediction accuracy. We detail the algorithm's design, including the introduction of a dynamic probability field and the mechanism for feedback incorporation. The paper concludes with a discussion of the algorithm's performance evaluation and potential applications in diverse fields.

title: Title: Multi-Scale Constraint Propagation in Neural Networks
abstract: This paper explores the integration of multi-scale constraint propagation techniques into neural networks, aiming to enhance learning and generalization capabilities. Traditional constraint propagation methods often restrict the scope of constraint application to a single scale, limiting the network's ability to effectively capture complex relationships within the input data and the network's representation. We propose a novel system that analyzes the network's representation at multiple scales, propagating constraints across these levels of detail. This allows for a more granular and comprehensive understanding of the input, leading to improved accuracy and robustness. The paper details the core mechanism, presents preliminary experimental results demonstrating improvements in accuracy and generalization, and discusses future research directions.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Data Compression via Waveform Analysis (QEDWA)
abstract: Quantum-Enhanced Data Compression via Waveform Analysis (QEDWA) presents a novel approach to data compression leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement. This research investigates the potential of harnessing quantum phenomena to identify and compress highly correlated data patterns, aiming to surpass the limitations of current classical compression techniques. The core mechanism centers on establishing a probabilistic basis for data representation through quantum entanglement, enabling a more efficient and robust compression process. This paper outlines the theoretical framework, experimental investigation, and preliminary results demonstrating the efficacy of QEDWA in achieving significantly higher compression ratios compared to established algorithms. We will address challenges related to quantum decoherence and entanglement management, while exploring the potential for future advancements in this rapidly evolving field.

title: Explainable Deep Reinforcement Learning for Safety System Design
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Explainable Deep Reinforcement Learning (XDRL) to enhance the design of safety systems. Traditional deep reinforcement learning (DRL) models, while effective in achieving optimal performance, often operate as black boxes, lacking transparency and trustworthiness – critical factors in safety-critical domains. This research addresses this limitation by proposing a novel framework that integrates DRL with explainable AI techniques. Specifically, we utilize a deep reinforcement learning model incorporating an attention mechanism, coupled with a rule-based engine, to provide interpretable decision-making processes. The core claim is that leveraging XDRL enables a deeper understanding of the underlying reasoning behind safety system actions, leading to more reliable and confident optimization recommendations. The proposed approach aims to bridge the gap between performance and interpretability, fostering greater trust and acceptance of DRL in safety-critical applications. We demonstrate the potential of this methodology through a theoretical analysis and outline a framework suitable for adaptation to various safety system designs.

title: Title: Adaptive Deep Learning Hyperparameter Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive deep learning hyperparameter optimization method designed to enhance model performance and training efficiency. Traditional hyperparameter optimization methods often rely on fixed, predetermined settings, which can be suboptimal in complex scenarios. This work proposes a novel approach that dynamically adjusts the hyperparameters of a deep learning model during the training process, leveraging the inherent adaptability of deep learning to optimize model behavior. The core mechanism focuses on a continuous, iterative adjustment of hyperparameters based on a learned model performance metric, ensuring a more refined and effective optimization strategy. The method demonstrates improved training speed and enhanced model accuracy compared to existing techniques.

title: Title: Automated Theorem Discovery via Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: This paper introduces an automated theorem discovery system powered by evolutionary algorithms, aiming to accelerate the process of mathematical research. The system leverages a genetic algorithm to generate novel mathematical theorems by iteratively refining a set of axioms and conjectures. The core mechanism centers around a criteria-based reward system that prioritizes novelty and explanatory power, driving the evolution of new mathematical statements. We present a framework demonstrating the potential for this approach to significantly improve the speed and efficiency of mathematical discovery, moving beyond human-curated theorem generation. The system's effectiveness is evaluated through a series of illustrative examples and preliminary results.

title: Cognitive Architectures Based on Predictive Coding and Hierarchical Abstraction
abstract: This paper proposes a novel cognitive architecture grounded in the principles of predictive coding and hierarchical abstraction. The architecture aims to simulate human cognition by implementing predictive coding mechanisms at multiple levels of abstraction, facilitating efficient information representation and processing. The core claim is that human cognition relies fundamentally on these mechanisms. The architecture's key innovation lies in its comprehensive implementation of predictive coding, coupled with a hierarchical structure designed for learning and anticipating future events based on accumulated experience. We detail the architecture's components, focusing on the feedback loops characteristic of predictive coding and the abstraction processes inherent in hierarchical systems. The model's potential applications span various cognitive domains, including perception, action, and learning, and provides a framework for investigating the neural basis of cognitive function. The architecture utilizes a layered approach, with lower layers focusing on raw sensory input and higher layers generating predictions that are then compared to incoming data. Discrepancies drive updates, refining both the predictions and the internal models. This iterative process allows the system to learn and adapt to changing environments, ultimately leading to a robust and efficient cognitive system.

title: 基于自适应的量子计算的非线性优化算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum optimization algorithm based on adaptive quantum computation, leveraging quantum entanglement and quantum simulation to efficiently solve non-linear optimization problems. Traditional optimization methods often suffer from computational limitations, necessitating substantial resources. This research introduces a dynamically adjusted quantum algorithm that exploits quantum entanglement and quantum simulation to achieve significantly improved performance compared to existing techniques. The core mechanism centers on a carefully designed quantum circuit architecture that utilizes entanglement to explore the solution space more effectively and efficiently. This paper details the algorithm's design, analysis of its performance, and potential applications across diverse non-linear optimization scenarios.

title: Non-Equilibrium Learning in Complex Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the application of non-equilibrium learning theory to complex networks. Traditional learning models often assume equilibrium conditions between learners and their environments, a simplification that may not hold true in complex networked systems where dynamics can be significantly different. We propose that incorporating non-equilibrium learning principles, specifically the presence of a dynamic disparity between learner and environment, can substantially enhance learning efficiency and robustness. The core of this approach involves simulating the non-equilibrium dynamics between a learner and the network environment, and subsequently designing tailored learning algorithms. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this framework, outlining key concepts and providing a foundational understanding for future research. The results presented suggest a novel method for tackling network learning challenges, offering a more realistic and potentially more effective approach compared to conventional equilibrium-based models.

title: Topological Quantum Computing Error Correction Code Optimization Algorithms
abstract: This paper investigates the optimization of error correction codes specifically tailored for topological quantum computing. Recognizing the unique challenges posed by error propagation within topological networks, we propose a novel approach centered on analyzing and mitigating error transmission pathways. The core of our method involves constructing a topological quantum computing model and simulating error propagation dynamics. Utilizing an optimization algorithm, we systematically adjust the parameters of the error correction code, aiming to reduce the velocity of error propagation and ultimately enhance the overall resilience of the topological quantum computation. We demonstrate the potential of this approach to significantly improve the fault tolerance of topological quantum computers. The primary mathematical framework revolves around the concept of topological entanglement entropy and its application in quantifying error propagation rates. The key equations used are: (Ei, t) representing the energy of a qubit at time t, (γij) representing the coupling strength between qubits i and j, (Pij) representing the probability of error propagation between qubits i and j, (Hij) representing the Hamiltonian operator governing the interaction between qubits i and j, (ρi) representing the density matrix of qubit i, and (Si) representing the topological entanglement entropy of qubit i. The optimization algorithm, a variant of the genetic algorithm, is defined as: (αij, βij) where αij and βij represent the parameters to be optimized, and the objective function is defined as minimizing (Pij) for all pairs of qubits i and j. The overall error correction fidelity is quantified as: (F) = 1 - (∑i Pi), where Pi is the probability of error for qubit i. This work contributes to the development of robust and scalable topological quantum computing architectures.

title: Measured agility: does an organisation's history of cryptographic change predict its post-quantum posture?
abstract: A behavioural measure of organisational cryptographic agility, built from 10.7 million Certificate Transparency records for 11,999 registrable domains sampled from the Tranco top 1M, and a pre-specified test of whether it predicts hybrid post-quantum TLS key exchange support. The predictor is a set of lead times against externally imposed deadlines: the Entrust distrust of November 2024, the reduction of maximum certificate validity to 200 days in March 2026, and elective ECDSA adoption. Because recent work finds that 93.92% of observed post-quantum deployments come from provider-managed configurations, the primary hypothesis is a moderated one: prior agility predicts current posture only where the domain owner controls the TLS configuration. This is the first predictive-validity test of any published crypto-agility construct.

title: Heat Field Signatures: From Point Clouds to Smooth Geometry
abstract: Bringing multiscale geometric analysis directly to irregular point clouds remains difficult: quantities such as local dimension, anisotropy, density variation, and geometric transitions are typically estimated through explicit neighborhood, manifold, or graph constructions, or left for neural networks to infer from coordinates. We introduce Heat Field Signatures (HFS), which lift a point cloud to a multiscale family of smooth ambient heat fields, providing a direct interface from discrete samples to geometric analysis. From this field, HFS computes closed-form global and local signatures directly from pairwise distances, capturing heat concentration, intrinsic dimension, anisotropy, and scale transitions. We further introduce the Heat Dimension Spectrum (HDS), a compact summary of multiscale geometric composition. HFS can be used as a closed-form descriptor, a lightweight learned representation, or a geometric feature channel for neural point-cloud models. Across synthetic and real-world benchmarks spanning subcellular, neuronal, tree, and protein data, HFS outperforms strong point-cloud and multiparameter-persistence baselines while substantially reducing end-to-end cost. On SCOP protein-fold classification, HFS improves over the strongest deep baseline by nearly $24$ percentage points using coordinates alone, while standalone HFS representations are exactly rotation-invariant by construction. More broadly, HFS turns a classical heat field into a practical interface for multiscale geometric analysis in modern point-cloud learning.

title: CNsEMD: An Expert-Annotated Multi-Field-Strength MRI Dataset and a Hyperspherical Manifold Network for Multimodal Cranial Nerve Parcellation
abstract: Cranial nerves (CNs) play essential roles in sensory, motor, and autonomic functions. Accurate CN parcellation from multimodal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is crucial for neuroanatomical analysis and neurosurgical planning. However, accurate CN parcellation remains extremely challenging because CNs are very small, exhibit low image contrast, and have slender tubular morphologies and complex anatomical trajectories. Moreover, the lack of publicly available, expert-annotated datasets has impeded the development and fair benchmarking of learning-based CN analysis methods. In this work, we introduce CNsEMD, an expert-annotated multimodal dataset for CN parcellation. It comprises data from 202 subjects acquired on 3T, 5T, and 7T MRI scanners. We further propose the projective hyperspherical manifold network (PHM-Net), which learns cross-modal representations by capturing angular relationships in a shared hyperspherical embedding space. Rather than performing multimodal fusion in Euclidean space, the proposed Hyperspherical cross-modal interaction (HCI) module enables bidirectional feature exchange between T1-weighted (T1w) and direction-encoded color (DEC) representations on a unit hypersphere. The Magnitude-preserving projective hyperspherical orientation representation (PHOR) captures the axial nature of DEC orientations while preserving diffusion magnitude. The hyperspherical prototype segmentation head (HPSH) further extends angular similarity to voxel-wise classification using normalized voxel embeddings and learnable class prototypes. Extensive experimental results on the CNsEMD dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our PHM-Net against state-of-the-art methods. CNsEMD establishes a reproducible benchmark for multimodal CN imaging, while PHM-Net provides a geometry-consistent solution for CN parcellation across diverse MRI acquisitions.

title: Enhancing Typo-Tolerant Data Retrieval in the Andeng Village PKK Information System Using the Damerau-Levenshtein Distance Algorithm
abstract: Data search is an essential feature in information systems that enables users to retrieve required information efficiently and accurately. However, the data search process in the Andeng Village Family Welfare Movement (PKK) Activity Management Information System is still limited because users must enter search queries that exactly match the stored data. Consequently, the system fails to retrieve relevant information when typographical errors (typos) occur in search queries. This study aims to improve the effectiveness of data retrieval by implementing the Damerau-Levenshtein Distance algorithm to support typo-tolerant searching, allowing the system to retrieve relevant data despite variations in user input. The algorithm was implemented by measuring the similarity between user queries and stored data using four edit operations, namely insertion, deletion, substitution, and transposition. The evaluation was conducted using 50 typo-containing search queries representing various typo patterns in PKK activity data, and the performance was measured based on retrieval accuracy and processing time. The results show that the implemented algorithm successfully retrieved relevant data despite typing errors in search queries. The testing achieved 100% accuracy on the tested PKK search scenarios with an average search processing time of 65.11 ms or 0.06511 seconds. These findings indicate that the Damerau-Levenshtein Distance algorithm provides effective and efficient performance for improving typo-tolerant data searching in the Andeng Village Family Welfare Movement (PKK) Activity Management Information System.

title: Quantum Chemistry Beyond DFT for Low-Activation Fusion Alloys: ADAPT-VQE Correlation Energies for Composition-of-Matter Screening with Fault-Tolerant Resource Estimates
abstract: Screening the low-activation alloys that make up a fusion reactor's plasma-facing and structural components by density-functional theory (DFT) runs into a wall: on the correlated 3d transition metals that constitute the family, the computed energetics depend on the exchange–correlation functional at the level of hundreds of millihartree, which is comparable to or larger than the composition differences the screen must resolve. A screen whose verdict changes with the functional is not a screen. We close that gap with an adaptive variational quantum eigensolver. We first set out the governing electronic-structure problem, the formal origin of the functional ambiguity, the well-posedness condition for a composition screen, the fermion-to-qubit mapping, and the ADAPT-VQE construction with its exact gradient-selection criterion and monotone-convergence property. We then report the frozen results of the Kronos de-risking campaign (register serial BR-SX-07): ADAPT-VQE reaches chemical accuracy on all four 3d-alloy fragments (Ti, V, Cr, Fe) with a residual below 0.05 mHa against a correlated reference — four orders of magnitude inside the 1.6 mHa (1 kcal mol^-1) chemical-accuracy threshold and four orders of magnitude tighter than the >300 mHa DFT functional spread it replaces — using adaptively grown circuits that are 4–14× shallower in two-qubit (CNOT) count than a unitary coupled-cluster (UCCSD) ansatz at equal accuracy. An independently reproduced four-qubit proof-of-concept validates the machinery to 3.9×10^-6 Ha against exact diagonalization. The results were produced on the NVIDIA GPU HPC campaign by classical statevector emulation of the quantum circuits, with plane-wave DFT and correlated quantum-chemistry references computed on the same fleet. We state the honest gate once and quantify it: this is not a claim of quantum advantage; a single-determinant ADAPT-VQE variant stalls at 24 mHa on the strongly multireference vacancy limit; and scaling from fragments to a full alloy or REBCO cell moves the problem into fault-tolerant quantum phase estimation, estimated at ~10^9 Toffoli gates and ~238 logical qubits (~38 days at a 1 kHz logical-Toffoli throughput). We place the method inside the honest-scoping grammar of the Kronos AI-and-quantum programme: the fragment ADAPT-VQE energetics are a twin-testable capability that runs today on classical hardware, the full-cell phase estimation is a horizon-class quantum task quoted against an explicit classical baseline, and every offline quantum kernel is benchmarked in qubits and non-Clifford (Toffoli/T) gate count with no crossover to the real-time control loop this decade. On the resulting ladder the alloy-chemistry phase estimation (~10^9 Toffoli) is the most tractable offline kernel — far below the equilibrium linear-solve (~10^17 T gates) and fleet-optimization (~10^19–10^23 T gates) kernels — and we report the matrix-product-state classical frontier it must beat. The deliverable is a validated, circuit-efficient electronic-structure tool for composition-of-matter screening today, with a resource-honest map of what the fault-tolerant extension will cost. Key results (frozen anchors): Q = 3.076; delta = -0.30; kappa = 2.0; p = 1; q = 1; s = 1. Methods & codes: OpenMC, VQE, ADAPT-VQE. Live verification: 2 gate validator(s) with live-recompute cards (2 reproduced). See the Verification section and data/verification.csv. Related: Paper page · De-risking register · 3D model · Learn more about Kronos Part of the 2026 Kronos publication series; independently re-run and stamped in the Kronos de-risking register (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22645689). All numerical values are frozen design-point anchors; see the register. Public research artifact. No proprietary, financial, or supply-chain information is included.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Dynamic Information Transmission
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon of quantum mechanics, presents a potentially revolutionary approach to information transmission. This paper explores the feasibility of utilizing quantum entanglement to create a dynamic information transmission system, offering enhanced security and efficiency compared to traditional methods. We propose a novel algorithm based on the manipulation of entangled states, demonstrating the potential of this technique for quantum communication and quantum computation. The core mechanism involves designing a system where the state of entangled particles can be dynamically adjusted, facilitating the transmission of complex information. This research investigates the practical challenges and theoretical underpinnings of this approach, highlighting its implications for advancing these fields. We will present a preliminary model demonstrating the core principles and potential applications of this dynamic information transmission system.

title: Dynamic Topology-Based Machine Learning Algorithm Prediction Evaluation
abstract: This paper presents a novel machine learning algorithm for evaluating the prediction accuracy and robustness of dynamic topology-based models. Traditional evaluation metrics often lack the nuanced understanding of dynamic topology's influence on model performance. We propose a new metric, termed "Dynamic Topology Prediction," that leverages the inherent properties of dynamic topology to assess algorithmic prediction capabilities. This metric incorporates a novel weighting scheme based on topology connectivity and stability, providing a more comprehensive assessment than existing methods. The study compares the Dynamic Topology Prediction metric with established machine learning techniques, demonstrating its efficacy in identifying and quantifying the strengths and weaknesses of dynamic topology-based models. The results highlight the potential of this new metric for improving the reliability and predictive power of dynamic topology algorithms.

title: Dynamic Topology Codes for Quantum Information: A Novel Approach to Enhanced Quantum Communication and Error Correction
abstract: This paper explores the utilization of dynamic topology maps as a novel framework for quantum information encoding, aiming to significantly enhance the efficiency of quantum communication and error correction. Quantum information is inherently susceptible to noise and decoherence, hindering practical applications. Dynamic topology maps, characterized by their topological robustness and adaptable structure, offer a promising solution. We investigate the potential of this approach to create more resilient and efficient quantum channels, reducing the need for complex error correction schemes. The core mechanism centers around leveraging the inherent properties of dynamic topology to improve the fidelity of quantum states and facilitate robust quantum communication. This work presents a conceptual framework and preliminary results demonstrating the feasibility of this technique, highlighting key advancements in utilizing topology to bolster quantum systems.

title: Context-Aware Graph Embedding with Semantic Layering
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to graph embedding that addresses the limitations of traditional methods by incorporating semantic information within the graph structure. We propose a "semantic layering" scheme that assigns nodes to different levels based on their relationships and properties, effectively creating a hierarchical representation of the graph. This layered approach is then leveraged to tailor graph embedding techniques, resulting in embeddings that are more sensitive to the semantic context of nodes and their connections. We demonstrate that this method significantly improves the quality and interpretability of graph embeddings compared to standard techniques. The core contribution lies in moving beyond purely structural considerations to capture meaningful semantic relationships within graph data. This allows for more effective downstream tasks such as node classification, link prediction, and knowledge graph reasoning. The paper outlines the methodology, the rationale behind the semantic layering, and the specific embedding techniques utilized. We provide a theoretical framework for understanding the impact of semantic layering on embedding effectiveness and present a conceptual overview of the system.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Propagation for Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum computing to revolutionize constraint propagation in optimization problems. Traditional constraint propagation methods often suffer from limitations in computational efficiency, particularly when dealing with complex, high-dimensional problems. We propose a novel approach leveraging quantum entanglement to enhance constraint propagation, aiming to dramatically improve the speed and accuracy of solving constrained optimization problems. The core mechanism involves establishing entanglement between constraint variables, enabling a more efficient and synchronized exploration of the search space. We detail the theoretical foundation, implementation details, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of this technique. The research focuses on addressing the computational bottleneck inherent in current optimization algorithms and presents a pathway towards significant advancements in the field.

title: 基于量子自联通的机器学习算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning algorithm, termed "Quantum Entanglement-Based Learning" (QEL), that leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to enhance the learning efficiency and generalization ability of machine learning models. Traditional machine learning approaches are inherently limited by classical computational constraints. Quantum entanglement offers a paradigm shift in computation, potentially enabling faster and more robust learning. We propose a QEL framework that utilizes entangled qubits to represent data and perform computations in a fundamentally different manner than conventional algorithms. This paper details the theoretical underpinnings, implementation details, and experimental results demonstrating the superiority of QEL across a range of benchmark datasets. The core mechanism of QEL relies on the ability of entangled qubits to exhibit correlated behavior, facilitating the exploration of complex data spaces and accelerating convergence toward optimal solutions. This work presents a significant advancement towards more efficient and accurate machine learning.

title: 基于自适应的拓扑自动化的算法框架
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for data compression and efficient transmission based on adaptive topology optimization. Traditional approaches to data compression often rely on manually designed transformations. This work introduces a novel algorithm that dynamically adjusts the topology of data structures, optimizing for specific characteristics and target structures. The core mechanism utilizes a combination of topological principles and adaptive optimization techniques to achieve enhanced compression and transfer efficiency. We explore the framework's capabilities through rigorous analysis and preliminary experiments, demonstrating its potential for significant improvements in data representation and transmission.

title: Algorithmic Quantum State Collapse Optimization (AQSCO)
abstract: This paper introduces Algorithmic Quantum State Collapse Optimization (AQSCO), a novel algorithm designed to enhance the efficiency of quantum measurements through a synergistic combination of statistical likelihood and quantum interference. Traditional collapse methods often rely on deterministic approaches, potentially leading to suboptimal results. AQSCO addresses this limitation by dynamically adjusting the collapse process based on probability distributions, optimizing for reduced measurement error. The core mechanism utilizes a 'statistical collapse gradient' technique, effectively guiding the quantum state towards a more stable and predictable outcome. This approach offers the potential for significantly improved measurement accuracy and a deeper understanding of quantum phenomena. We present a comprehensive theoretical framework and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating the efficacy of AQSCO in a series of quantum state collapse experiments.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Dynamic Geometry Topology (QEDT)
abstract: Quantum Entanglement-Based Dynamic Geometry Topology (QEDT) is a novel approach to understanding and manipulating geometric topology, leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement to dynamically explore and optimize complex structures. This paper introduces a method that utilizes entangled states to learn and analyze geometric topology, specifically focusing on the potential to optimize the resulting structures through a dynamic process. The core mechanism centers around the observation that entangled states allow for the exploration of multiple possibilities simultaneously, enabling a more efficient and nuanced understanding of topological properties. The proposed QEDT framework offers a fundamentally different perspective on geometric topology, moving beyond static analysis towards a dynamic, entangled exploration of structure. This work explores the potential for this approach to unlock new insights into the behavior of complex geometric systems.

This paper introduces a method that utilizes entangled states to learn and analyze geometric topology, specifically focusing on the potential to optimize the resulting structures through a dynamic process. The core mechanism centers around the observation that entangled states allow for the exploration of multiple possibilities simultaneously, enabling a more efficient and nuanced understanding of topological properties. The proposed QEDT framework offers a fundamentally different perspective on geometric topology, moving beyond static analysis towards a dynamic, entangled exploration of structure. This work explores the potential for this approach to unlock new insights into the behavior of complex geometric systems.

title: Title: Dynamic Lattice-Based Representation of Quantum States
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic lattice-based representation for quantum states, designed to optimize representation and analysis through adaptive lattice structure adjustment. Traditional lattice methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their applicability to specific quantum systems. Our approach dynamically adjusts the connectivity and spacing of the lattice, allowing the representation to adapt to the unique properties of the underlying system. The core mechanism involves analyzing the system's characteristics and modifying the lattice structure accordingly. This adaptive approach significantly enhances the fidelity of quantum state representations, leading to improved analysis and computational efficiency. The design incorporates a mechanism to automatically determine optimal lattice parameters, reducing the need for manual parameter tuning. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through simulations and preliminary analysis of specific quantum systems, highlighting its superior performance compared to static lattice representations.

title: 自适应拓扑的量子计算几何优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum computing geometric optimization algorithm based on adaptive topology. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex geometric structures, hindering the potential for enhanced quantum computation. Our approach leverages the inherent properties of quantum topology to dynamically adapt the optimization process, leading to improved efficiency and solution quality. The core mechanism involves mapping the geometric optimization problem to a quantum-mechanical representation, utilizing quantum algorithms to represent and manipulate the topology, ultimately optimizing the solution space. We present a preliminary implementation demonstrating the effectiveness of this method on a specific geometric optimization task, highlighting its potential for advancing quantum algorithm design and efficiency.

title: Resilient physiological control under side-channel compromise for IoMT devices
abstract: The rapid expansion of the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) has exposed life critical devices to microarchitectural side-channel attacks capable of bypassing traditional cryptographic protections. Timing-based and cache-based leakage can enable an adversary to recover private keys or infer administrative credentials, allowing malicious commands to appear digitally authentic while remaining physiologically unsafe. This work introduces a dual-layer physio-side-channel defense architecture designed to maintain patient safety even under full digital compromise. At the signal-processing layer, a Denoising Autoencoder (DAE) reconstructs telemetry corrupted by controlled perturbation models that emulate side-channel induced distortions, restoring classification performance from failure levels ( \(\approx \) 28%) to near baseline accuracy. At the actuation layer, a Control Barrier Function (CBF) enforces formal safety constraints on cardiac pacing, ensuring that unsafe but cryptographically valid commands cannot drive the physiological state outside clinically acceptable bounds. Experimental validation using VGG16-based feature extraction and ART-generated adversarial perturbations demonstrates robust performance across three representative attack vectors: side-timing leakage, cache-timing interference, and password-timing inference. While offline training incurs a substantial computational cost ( \(\approx \) 7387.61 s), real-time inference operates within sub-second latency, supporting deployment on embedded IoMT gateway hardware. Together, these results establish a safety architecture for next-generation medical cyber-physical systems.

title: A Sub-4 Approximation for Fair $k$-Means
abstract: Fairness in clustering has attracted sustained research interest, motivated by the need to ensure equitable representation of protected groups in machine learning applications. We study fair $k$-means clustering in Euclidean space, where the proportion of each protected group in every cluster must lie within specified lower and upper bounds. These constraints make it challenging to determine both cluster centers and point assignments. We propose an approximation algorithm that combines a linear programming relaxation with geometric transformations of the input to construct candidate center sets. Given a $ρ$-approximate algorithm for weighted $k$-means and any $ε>0$, our algorithm returns a fractional solution whose cost is at most $1+(3-1/Γ)ρ+O(ε)$ times the optimal integral fair cost, where $Γ\approx6.357$ is an upper bound on the integrality gap of the standard Euclidean $k$-means LP. With a PTAS as the subroutine, the approximation ratio becomes $3.8427+O(ε)$, improving the previous factor of $5+O(ε)$ to below $4$. The solution satisfies all fairness constraints exactly and can be rounded to an integral assignment with a bounded additive violation of fairness and no increase in cost. The same approximation guarantee extends to the $k$-sparse Wasserstein barycenter problem.

title: Thermodynamic Cyclic Processes with Markov Samplers in Bayesian Inference
abstract: The concept of Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) cycles, an analogy to cyclic processes in heat engines, is presented in order to examine Bayesian inference problems. In this effort, we develop adaptive ensemble schedulers that allow the tuning of external parameters of a Bayesian canonical ensemble during an MCMC run, realising the MCMC cycles in practice. We run these cycles on different statistical models. As a fundamental insight, we find (both theoretically and in practice) that such systems can produce a non-zero net work output if and only if the considered model is non-Gaussian. As such, they may serve as a measure of non-Gaussianity in Bayesian inference, which we test on an example from supernova cosmology.

title: PV-WM: A Heterogeneous Micro-Macro World Model for Articulated Pedestrian-Vehicle Co-Rollout
abstract: Local pedestrian-vehicle forecasting spans heterogeneous physical scales: pedestrians combine root locomotion with articulated motion, whereas vehicles are rigid bodies described by kinematic state and oriented extent. Existing road-agent forecasters typically omit pedestrian articulation, while pose forecasters leave vehicle futures outside the learned rollout. We introduce PV-WM, a history-only world model over structured post-perception tracks. It recurrently advances pedestrian root motion, 15-joint articulation, and learned vehicle states within a synchronized heterogeneous state. The generated pedestrian and vehicle chunks supply the next recurrent boundary; vehicle boxes are reconstructed from predicted center and heading with observed extent, and P-V geometry is recomputed after every transition. Relative to a matched one-shot complete-state predictor, recurrent execution reduces Root ADE by 12.7% and MPJPE by 14.8%. Feedback interventions show that later predictions depend on the content, temporal order, and pedestrian identity of generated articulation. Across 824 aligned Waymo contexts, with 797 providing valid future vehicle support, PV-WM reduces Root ADE by 5.2%, MPJPE by 7.6%, P-V distance error by 11.9%, and oriented-box closest-approach error by 5.8% relative to a validation-selected Modular Specialist. The single-network model uses 57.1% fewer parameters, 96.5% lower average FLOPs per local scene, and 25.5% lower measured p95 latency. PV-WM unifies this heterogeneous future state while preserving type-specific pedestrian and vehicle dynamics.

title: Hiện tượng “ảo giác trí tuệ nhân tạo” và nguy cơ vi phạm sở hữu trí tuệ - Trách nhiệm pháp lý trong môi trường số và một số kiến nghị hoàn thiện quy định pháp luật
abstract: The phenomenon of “AI hallucinations” occurs when artificial intelligence (AI) generates false or fabricated information, leading to potential risks of intellectual property (IP) infringement. This issue raises critical questions regarding the legal liability of stakeholders, including AI developers, intermediary AI service providers, and end-users. Based on this context, the article analyzes Vietnam’s current intellectual property laws, identifies existing legal gaps, and consults the international experiences of several countries. Consequently, the paper proposes recommendations to refine legal regulations, ensuring a harmonious balance between technological advancement and the protection of IP rights in the digital era.

title: Warmup Hurts: A Two-Stage Schedule Ablation and Physical-Perturbation Robustness Analysis of Lion in PPO
abstract: رغم استمرار AdamW كمُحسِّن افتراضي لخوارزمية PPO، فإن حالته اللحظية ذات المخزنين (ذاكرة 2P) تُكلّف ضعف ما يتطلبه المُحسِّن القائم على الإشارة Lion (1P). غير أن مقدار تحديث Lion يتتبّع معدل التعلم اللحظي بشكل مباشر وحصري، دون أي آلية تقوم مقام التطبيع الذاتي الداخلي لـ AdamW عند تراجع الجدول الزمني؛ وهو ما يجعله عرضة بنيويًا لظاهرة الرفرفة (chattering)، وينبغي أن يجعل تنافسيته مع AdamW حساسة للجدول الزمني بخلاف AdamW. نعزل هذه الحساسية عبر دراسة استئصال من مرحلتين على PPO في أربع بيئات تحكم مستمر من MuJoCo (HalfCheetah-v4، Walker2d-v4، Ant-v4، Hopper-v4؛ 15 بذرة عشوائية لكل تهيئة، باستخدام اختبار Welch's t مع تصحيح Holm-Bonferroni)، حيث نُحلّل ثلاث تهيئات لـ Lion (lion_raw: بلا جدول زمني؛ lion_cosine: تراجع جيبي منذ البداية؛ lion_warmup_cosine: إحماء خطي وهضبة ثم التراجع الجيبي نفسه) إلى مقارنتين مستقلتين ومتراكمتين. في البيئات الثلاث المستقرة سلبيًا (HalfCheetah-v4، Walker2d-v4، Ant-v4)، يكون التراجع مفيدًا بينما الإحماء ضارًا بشكل معنوي، إذ يُخفّض متوسط العائد بنسبة 39-55% ويزيد الرفرفة بنسبة 12-18% مقارنة بالتراجع وحده، ويتأكد هذا النمط الاتجاهي - المعكوس بالنسبة للإحماء، عكس مبرره المعتاد في التعلم الخاضع للإشراف - في إنتروبيا السياسة بعد التدريب. أما في بيئة Hopper-v4 الأقل استقرارًا، فلا يصل أي استئصال منفرد إلى الدلالة الإحصائية، رغم أن المقارنة المجمّعة بين lion_raw وlion_warmup_cosine تصل إليها. كما نُقدّم تحليلًا استكشافيًا بعديًا لمتانة الاضطراب الفيزيائي (زيادة الكتلة، ضوضاء الاستشعار): يتراوح متوسط استعادة العائد بعد إعادة الضبط الدقيق بين 54.7% (الأسوأ، Walker2d-v4) و113.7% (الأفضل، Ant-v4، وهو تحسّن فعلي)، ويبدو أنه محكوم بخاصية مختلفة عن الاستقرار السلبي في الحالة النظيفة.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Error Correction (AQEC) - Dynamic Error Resilience
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for revolutionizing various fields, but its inherent fragility necessitates robust error correction techniques. Traditional methods often struggle to effectively handle the complex and variable errors that arise during quantum operations. This paper introduces Adaptive Quantum Error Correction (AQEC), a novel approach that dynamically adjusts correction parameters based on real-time error rate analysis, offering a significantly improved level of reliability. The core mechanism involves a continuous monitoring and correction process, adapting to the unique characteristics of each quantum system. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this system through simulations and preliminary experimental results, highlighting its potential to overcome limitations of existing error correction methods.

title: Formal Semantics and Program Generation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to program generation based on formal semantics and automated reasoning. The core idea is to represent programs as formal structures and leverage formal methods for automated generation. Unlike traditional program synthesis techniques that rely on hand-crafted rules, this work utilizes logic programming and theorem proving to achieve a more robust and verifiable generation process. The system translates programs into a formal language, allowing for logical inference and automated deduction. This results in a systematic method for program generation, minimizing the reliance on heuristics and maximizing the guarantee of correctness. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a theoretical framework, outlining the key components and their interactions. The focus is on establishing a solid theoretical foundation for program generation, paving the way for more reliable and scalable automated software development.

title: 基于自适应神经网络的复杂系统模拟
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for complex system simulation utilizing an adaptive neural network (ANN). Traditional simulation methods often rely on manually designed models, while this approach leverages ANNs for automated and flexible simulation. The core innovation lies in the ANN's ability to dynamically adjust system parameters based on learned relationships, resulting in improved efficiency and accuracy in simulating complex systems. This work addresses the limitations of traditional simulation techniques by offering a more adaptable and potentially more accurate approach to modeling dynamic systems. This framework focuses on learning the system's internal dynamics through an ANN, enabling automated parameter tuning and improved simulation fidelity. The results demonstrate significant improvements in simulation accuracy and speed compared to conventional methods, particularly in simulating systems with complex interactions.

title: 基于自适应高阶矩阵的量子算法优化
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum algorithm optimization framework based on adaptive high-order matrices. Traditional quantum algorithm optimization often relies on static parameter adjustments, limiting its applicability to complex algorithms. Our proposed method dynamically adjusts high-order matrix parameters to optimize quantum algorithm performance, thereby significantly enhancing computational efficiency. We detail the framework's architecture, explain the key optimization strategy, and provide illustrative examples demonstrating its effectiveness across a range of quantum algorithms. The core mechanism lies in the iterative refinement of high-order matrix configurations to achieve optimal performance.

title: Dynamic Code Generation for Adaptive Cryptographic Protocols
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to cryptographic protocol design, centered around dynamic code generation. Traditional cryptographic protocols are often static, relying on pre-defined algorithms and parameters, which can be vulnerable to evolving threats and network conditions. This work introduces a system that leverages a code generation engine to dynamically adapt cryptographic algorithms and parameters at runtime, informed by observed network behavior and identified security vulnerabilities. The core claim is that this adaptive approach can significantly enhance both the security and efficiency of cryptographic protocols. The system employs a runtime monitoring component to detect anomalies and potential attacks, feeding this information to the code generation engine. The engine then modifies the protocol logic, potentially switching to stronger algorithms, adjusting key sizes, or implementing countermeasures tailored to the specific situation. This paper outlines the architecture, key components, and potential benefits of this dynamic code generation framework, presenting a viable path towards more resilient and adaptable cryptographic systems. title: Quantum State Dynamics: A Novel Adaptive Optimization Approach
abstract: Quantum state dynamics represent a significant advancement in quantum computation, offering the potential for enhanced qubit coherence and increased computational power. However, the inherent complexity of quantum systems necessitates sophisticated optimization techniques to achieve optimal performance. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, Adaptive Optimization Based on Dynamic Quantum State Distributions, designed to dynamically adjust the probability distribution of quantum states based on system feedback. The core mechanism leverages a feedback loop to continuously refine the state distribution, improving both performance and stability. This approach contrasts with traditional optimization methods which operate on static probability distributions, promising a more robust and adaptable framework for quantum system design. This work explores the mathematical foundations and practical implementation of this algorithm, demonstrating its effectiveness through simulations and preliminary experiments. The focus is on enhancing quantum state coherence and exploring the potential for improved computational outcomes.

abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre yet fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for revolutionizing machine learning. This paper explores the design of a novel machine learning algorithm leveraging quantum entanglement to enhance model learning efficiency and generalization capabilities. We propose a framework centered around manipulating quantum states to facilitate complex pattern recognition and data representation, ultimately offering a potential paradigm shift in machine learning. We detail the underlying principles, mathematical modeling, and implementation considerations of this algorithm. The core claim underscores the transformative potential of this approach, highlighting its ability to overcome limitations inherent in classical machine learning. This work presents a preliminary investigation into the feasibility and potential benefits of applying quantum entanglement to enhance machine learning.

title: Quantum-Assisted Constraint Relaxation (QARC)
abstract: Quantum-Assisted Constraint Relaxation (QARC) is a novel technique for iteratively relaxing constraint parameters within a system, employing quantum fluctuations to accelerate convergence. The core mechanism centers around a 'quantum-induced relaxation' algorithm, utilizing quantum tunneling to identify optimal parameter values. This approach offers a significant advantage over traditional constraint relaxation methods, particularly in scenarios requiring rapid iteration and precise parameter settings. This paper presents a detailed explanation of the QARC algorithm, its underlying principles, and its potential impact on computational efficiency and solution quality across a range of modeling applications. We detail the quantum-tunneling process, the iterative refinement loop, and the resulting improvements in convergence speed and accuracy. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions, including exploring the integration of QEC with other optimization techniques.

title: Dynamic Symbolic Regression via Evolutionary Grammatical Inference
abstract: Symbolic regression is a powerful technique for discovering mathematical equations from data. However, it often struggles with complex datasets characterized by high dimensionality and inherent ambiguity in symbolic representations. This paper proposes a novel approach, Dynamic Symbolic Regression via Evolutionary Grammatical Inference (DSR-EGI), that addresses these limitations by employing an evolutionary algorithm to dynamically refine a grammar representing the target function. The core idea is to evolve a grammar not just based on the fitness of the functions it generates, but also on the structure of the grammar itself, favoring simpler, more compact representations. This dynamic adaptation allows the system to escape local optima and explore a broader range of potential solutions. The algorithm iteratively generates functions from the grammar, evaluates their fitness against the data, and then uses evolutionary pressure – specifically, graph-based pruning and expansion – to guide the evolution of the grammar. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of DSR-EGI in discovering accurate equations from challenging datasets, showcasing its ability to overcome the limitations of traditional symbolic regression. The system's adaptability and its incorporation of graph structure represent a significant advancement in the field.

title: Fractal Information Encoding for Neural Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neural network training that leverages fractal dimension as a foundational encoding metric. The core idea is to construct neural networks capable of effectively representing complex, hierarchical data by explicitly incorporating fractal geometry. We introduce embedding layers designed to recursively decompose input data into increasingly smaller, fractal-like representations. A learned fractal dimension parameter governs the scale and detail of this decomposition at each level. This method moves beyond conventional hierarchical representations, enabling networks to capture scale-invariant relationships and intricate self-similarity within data. The theoretical underpinnings and proposed architecture are detailed, outlining the potential for significant improvements in network performance across diverse applications. The key contribution lies in the systematic integration of fractal geometry into the network architecture, offering a new paradigm for neural network design. The proposed framework aims to address limitations of existing methods by providing a more robust and flexible approach to representing complex, multi-scale data.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Non-Asymmetric Computation Model
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers the potential for revolutionary computational capabilities. This paper explores a novel non-asymmetric computation model predicated on the intricate interplay of entangled states. We propose a mechanism centered around "quantum jumps" – probabilistic transformations of entangled qubits – that dramatically enhance the efficiency of certain algorithms. The core claim is that this model, through carefully engineered entanglement dynamics, offers a significant advancement over existing approaches, particularly in terms of computational complexity and speed. We detail the model's design, mathematical foundations, and potential implications for various computational tasks. This work represents a fundamental step towards harnessing the power of entanglement for practical applications.

title: 基于自适应的量子态控制的拓扑网络优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum state control leveraging adaptive quantum state manipulation for improved quantum information transmission and processing. Traditional methods often require manual design, limiting flexibility and potentially hindering performance. Our proposed framework employs a self-adjusting quantum state control strategy, allowing the system to dynamically optimize the quantum state within a specified network topology. We demonstrate the efficacy of this method through a series of simulations and analyses, showcasing significant improvements in quantum entanglement generation and fidelity compared to existing optimization techniques. The core mechanism focuses on a continuous feedback loop that adjusts the quantum state based on measured outcomes, enabling automated parameter tuning. This results in a more robust and adaptable quantum network, ultimately leading to enhanced quantum information transfer and processing capabilities.

title: Adaptive Probabilistic Logical Reasoning (APLR)
abstract: This paper introduces Adaptive Probabilistic Logical Reasoning (APLR), a novel approach to enhancing logical reasoning systems. The core idea is to develop a system capable of dynamically adjusting probabilistic logical reasoning rules based on environmental feedback. The system leverages a Bayesian network to construct a probabilistic logical reasoning model and employs reinforcement learning to train a controller. This controller adapts the rules based on the reasoning outcomes and the received environmental feedback, aiming to improve both accuracy and efficiency. The proposed method combines the strengths of probabilistic reasoning and reinforcement learning, offering a flexible and adaptive solution for complex reasoning tasks. The paper details the framework, the underlying mathematical principles, and the core mechanisms driving the APLR system, providing a foundational understanding for future development and applications.

title: RAG-basierte SQL-Agenten im Unternehmenseinsatz: Architektur, Evaluation und praktische Implikationen für einen demokratisierten Datenbankzugriff
abstract: Zusammenfassung Der Zugriff auf Unternehmensdaten über natürlichsprachliche Anfragen verspricht eine Demokratisierung der Datenbankinteraktion für nicht-technische Nutzer. Dieser Beitrag untersucht die Möglichkeiten und Grenzen von Text-to-SQL-Agenten (Structured Query Language, SQL), die auf Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) basieren und mit dem No-Code-Framework RAGFlow implementiert wurden. Hierfür wurden drei Prototypen für unterschiedliche Anwendungsfälle entwickelt: ein operativer Agent für Lagerabfragen, ein analytischer Agent für Vertriebskennzahlen und ein Beratungsagent für externe Kunden mit integrierten Datenschutzmechanismen. Die Evaluation zeigt ein differenziertes Bild: Für operative, faktenbasierte Anfragen erreichten die Prototypen Aufgabenerfolgsraten von 80–94 %. Ein zweistufiger Retrieval-Ansatz sowie ein Lookup-Mechanismus zur Fehlerkorrektur erhöhten die Robustheit für derartige Abfragen gegenüber unpräzisen Eingaben erheblich. Komplexe analytische Abfragen zeigten hingegen eine deutlich geringere Zuverlässigkeit (56–67 %), vor allem aufgrund von Kontextbegrenzungen der eingesetzten Large Language Models (LLMs) und Prioritätskonflikten zwischen Nutzer-Prompts und System-Prompts. Für die Praxis lässt sich ableiten, dass RAG-basierte SQL-Agenten bereits für Standardanfragen sinnvoll einsetzbar sind, während dedizierte Business-Intelligence-Tools (BI-Tools) für komplexe Analysen weiterhin überlegen bleiben. Der Beitrag liefert zudem konkrete architektonische Entscheidungen und Kriterien, die als Orientierung für die Implementierung solcher Agenten in Unternehmen dienen können.

title: Who Pays for Open Review? Visible Author Reputation and Its Effect on Ratings
abstract: An OpenReview bug in November 2025 broke anonymity at several conferences and prompted calls for open review, which motivate us to ask what shifting from blind to open would mean for authors. Analyzing over 18,000 reviewed submissions to ICLR 2026, split into de facto open and blind groups by arXiv preprint timing, we find that ratings rise with author reputation under both mechanisms, with a steeper slope under open review that is statistically significant, and that the open-blind difference is concentrated at the borderline ratings. The pattern holds across five reputation proxies (including institution, h-index, and citation count), three author-aggregation rules, and five definitions of the open window. A controlled simulation with five AI models as reviewers, holding the manuscript fixed and varying the author reputation, reproduces the effect. With claude-opus-5 as the reviewer, for example, rating rises by 0.5 points as the author moves from low to high reputation.

title: Online Surrogate Repair: Decoupling High-Fidelity Feedback from Search Length in Closed-Loop Discovery
abstract: Closed-loop AI scientists can generate candidate designs at low marginal computational cost, whereas reliable feedback may require wet-lab synthesis, characterization, or high-fidelity computation. Addressing this imbalance through custom laboratory automation remains infrastructure-intensive and costly, while replacing new experiments with a fixed surrogate leaves persistent model errors that can be amplified by optimization. We propose \emph{online surrogate repair} (OSR), a closed-loop algorithm that uses sparse high-fidelity evaluations to update the surrogate throughout a longer agent search conducted primarily with inexpensive surrogate feedback. An acquisition rule selects which designs from the agent's accumulated proposals receive high-fidelity evaluation, and the resulting labels update the surrogate used in subsequent episodes. Across controlled synthetic environments, we demonstrate that improving global surrogate fit does not necessarily reduce maximum regret, whereas Q90-UCB and expected improvement (EI) substantially reduce regret by directing evaluations toward regions that determine the optimizer's decisions. On MADE, controls receiving high-fidelity feedback after every episode require $6.36$--$7.23\times$ more oracle queries to match Online EI under two LLM orchestrators and $10.27\times$ more under the non-LLM Chemeleon+MLIP workflow. Online surrogate repair introduces a novel third feedback regime between fixed-surrogate operation and high-fidelity feedback after every episode, separating the frequency of high-fidelity evaluation from the duration of the agent's search.

title: Wavelength-Uniform Quantum Algorithms for Mixed-State Quantum Dynamics
abstract: One of the main challenges in numerical simulation of quantum dynamics is the prohibitive cost in the semi-classical regime, in which the de Broglie wave length is small compared with the characteristic length scale and the solution is highly oscillatory. For the von-Neumann equation for mixed-state quantum dynamics, this difficulty is overcome by using the Weyl variables, under which the solution is not oscillatory. Furthermore, we use the integral representation of the potential difference, which robustly captures the classical limit as the semi-classical parameter approaches zero. By using exact Hermite moments and quantum singular value transformation to treat the polynomial and sparse coordinate matrices of the dense projected smooth non-polynomial potentials respectively, we obtain a quantum algorithm efficient for {\it all} ranges of wave lengths, with complexity {\it polynomial} in the spatial dimension and discretization and query bounds containing {\it no} negative powers of the small wavelength. Thus it can capture the correct physical observables even if the spatial grid does not resolve the frequency, hence defying the Nyquist-Shannon sampling theorem.
